title: A6 generation-staged full rebuild + per-repo write locks (V043) (memory-sync phase A6)
body:
A6 of the global-DB consolidation (A1/V038..A5/V042; PR #416 — five P2 batches, 17 findings, + the coverage barrier incident, all in ONE commit 35891d7 on origin/main e5536e6). A full rebuild STAGES a fresh `files.generation` in CHUNKED per-wave transactions, then publishes via ONE TERMINAL transaction. LATEST 42->43; MIGRATION_043 arms in all three recognizers (`sha256:rag-rat-files-generation-v43`).

V043 = `apply_files_generation`: sentinel `column_exists(files,generation)`; FK-OFF self-wrapped txn; DROP files_new torn re-convergence; `generation INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`; UNIQUE -> (repo_id,path,commit_sha,worktree_id,generation); id verbatim. NO sole-repo backfill (repo-neutral; pointer absent=>0). First rebuild publishes generation 1.

RUNTIME. repo_meta[live_files_generation] pointer; registry.rs live_files_generation/active_generation (context else live fallback); active_generation stamped on every file INSERT. set_context_at_generation = rebuild seam. EVERY connection resolves `files` through a generation view: write_scope_view (config opens), write_repo_generation_view (BARE opens — repo+generation only, preserves #360; the MCP read path).

*** TERMINAL-FLIP + ROWS-INERT/CURSORS-LAST: the flip is the LAST fallible write; bulky KEYED rows may land pre-terminal ONLY when readers treat cursors/meta as authority. AUTHORITY set riding the flip: live_files_generation (last), indexed_at_ms, model seed, graph/flags marks, parser_failures staged apply, git_commit/git_dirty + git_history_indexed_* cursors (rows land Phase 2 via apply_prepared_git_history_deferring_cursors), and — batch 5 — repo_meta[source_root] (fs-fallback authority for memory validation/heals; the rebuild sets only the IN-MEMORY root early; a failed rebuild from a NEW checkout leaves old readers on the OLD root; audit found no further early authority keys — the FTS freshness trio is global infrastructure). Phase-3 order: carry_forward -> per carried overlay view-swap+resolve_overlay_edges -> restore base -> rebuild_logical_symbols -> apply_staged_parser_failures -> marks -> source_root + git meta + cursors -> pointer + seed -> COMMIT. Tests: a_tail_failure_leaves_the_old_generation_live..., ..._git_meta_and_history_cursors_on_the_old_state, ..._source_root_on_the_old_checkout, carried_overlay_edges_re_resolve... ***

*** CANONICAL LOCK ORDER (batch 5, SUPERSEDES the role-based incoming-then-outgoing argument — it broke when the fence-gap writer appeared with roles reversed): multi-per-repo-lock flows sort ids by `locks::canonical_lock_order` (lexicographic on the sanitized discriminator; locks.rs module doc owns the rule) and acquire in that order from a clean slate; an acquisition violating the order (earlier-sorting lock wanted while a later-sorting one is pre-held — unavoidable since entry locks are taken identity-blind) MUST be BOUNDED (acquire_timeout, never blocking): in-order unbounded edges cannot cycle under a total order, and any cycle containing a bounded edge self-breaks within the timeout as a retryable refusal. register_repo's upgrade acquires BOTH ids' locks in canonical order (reentrant-instant for a held entry lock), guards through commit. ***

*** FENCE GAP (batch 5): a writer's held lock must match the repo id it writes under. Entry locks key off the PRE-open derived id; an unshallow between derivation and adoption resolves+upgrades to portable — the writer would keep writing portable rows under only the stale local: lock. Fix: adopt_repo_from_config detects "thread holds SOME rag-rat-write-* lock for this DB (locks::thread_holds_any_repo_write_lock) but NOT the resolved id's (thread_holds_write_lock)" and stashes the resolved id's lock in IndexDatabase._identity_lock for the CONNECTION'S LIFETIME (bounded acquire; timeout = retryable "identity changed; re-run"). Lockless openers stay lockless. Test: a_writer_whose_identity_upgrades_mid_run_extends_its_lock_to_the_resolved_id (repo_registry.rs). ***

*** LOCK-HELD => NO IN-FLIGHT REBUILD => FULL RECLAMATION (batch 5, supersedes the batch-3 `< live` predicate): gc deadness is `generation != live` UNDER A DOCUMENTED FLOCK PRECONDITION — every production rebuild entry runs under the per-repo flock (CLI index, watcher/maintenance; verified — only tests call library rebuild() bare, and the test harness spawn_paused_rebuild now acquires it too), so a collector HOLDING the flock (Cmd::Gc belt, maintenance, watcher — all verified holders) knows above-live rows are ABANDONED staging from failed rebuilds (which `< live` could never reclaim — a persistently failing tail leaked a staged copy per retry). A flock-less embedded collector must use the lockless-safe `< live` form; do not silently weaken the precondition. Allocator still guarantees staging above live (max(row-MAX, live)+1). Tests: gc_reclaims_abandoned_staged_generations_from_failed_rebuilds, gc_serializes_on_the_flock_while_a_rebuild_is_mid_flight. ***

*** PARSER_FAILURES = STAGED-UNTIL-PUBLISH: temp.rebuild_parser_failures via graph.is_some(); apply in terminal; orphan sweep judges BASE scope at target and excludes staged upserts (PREPARE failures have no file row). StagedSweep{DeadContext,DeadGeneration} keeps the cascade off it on the generation axis. GENERATION-BOUNDED DELETES: remove_file_in_scope + heal_stale probes carry the writer's generation. FTS RACE: ensure_fts_fresh defers while any chunk HAS an fts row but NO chunk_text row. EVERY-APPLY-PATH SCHEMA LOCK: apply_schema_under_lock (double-checked, global rag-rat-schema.lock) in create_or_migrate + migrate_with_fastembed_cache + open_and_migrate. ***

*** INTERLEAVED WRITERS (proof at the per-wave commit, incremental.rs): (a) disjoint-table (MCP memory) — safe by disjointness + re-anchor lifecycle; (b) files-adjacent — generation discipline (bounded deletes, flock-preconditioned deadness, universal views); (c) schema appliers — global schema lock; (d) identity flux — canonical-order dual locks + the _identity_lock stash. ***

EXACTNESS vs DRIFT raw main.* reads: EXACT (generation predicate): all_symbols, rebuild_logical_symbols, call_path_edge_relocatable, refresh_clone_token_df, summary_counts graph_edges, ensure_graph_index_current wipe, overlay tombstone probe, heal_stale probes. DRIFT (re-justified in code): lexical graph_boost, delete_repo_chunk_blame.

TEST SEAM: barrier keyed BY DATABASE PATH + RAII WaveBarrierGuard (never process-global — libtest/coverage; class in the extended #409 flock memory; repro `taskset -c 0,1 cargo test`). spawn_paused_rebuild holds the production flock. Unrelated taskset flake: openai embed ordering, #417.

FALLOUT RULES: fixtures inserting into main.files post-rebuild stamp db.active_generation; "rebuild clears X" tests gc after (with flock); non-git counts via the view; tip pins at V043; poison sibling files at generation 0; reader-consistency moves ONLY the generation axis.

Gates (final): nextest --workspace 1527 passed; clippy clean; +nightly fmt --check clean; taskset gen-suite (20 tests) 3/3 + lock/upgrade tests clean. HANDOFF A7 importer: do NOT set live_files_generation (absent=>0); register_repo goes multi-repo — revisit the single-incumbent upgrade guard, keep the canonical-order + outgoing-lock + fence-gap rules. A8: per-repo locks + flock-preconditioned dead-gen gc + the interleaving suite make the concurrent index-A/write-B matrix meaningful.

title: flock released by fd-close alone outlives Drop when a sibling thread forks — unlock explicitly (#409)
body:
FileLock (crates/rag-rat-core/src/locks.rs) uses std's native file locks (File::lock/try_lock/unlock, stable ≥1.89 → flock on Unix). flock ownership belongs to the OPEN-FILE-DESCRIPTION, not the fd. So if you release the lock only by letting the fd close on Drop, and ANY other thread forks a child while the lock is held (any std::process::Command — the sibling tests shell out to `git`), the child inherits a duplicate reference to the same OFD. CLOEXEC closes fds only at exec, so through the whole fork→exec window the OFD stays alive despite the parent's close, and the flock survives the parent's drop() until the child execs. A try_acquire landing in that window sees WouldBlock.

SYMPTOM (#409): commands::index_ops::tests::maintenance_coalesces_a_concurrent_trigger flaked ONLY in the coverage job (plain `cargo test` under llvm-cov: many libtest threads in ONE process + git-forking sibling tests). Its second maintenance() coalesced after drop(held) because the FileLock's flock was still held via a fork-inherited OFD. nextest is immune (process-per-test → no in-process sibling forks), which is why only the coverage lane saw it. The same mechanism silently widens SQLITE_BUSY windows for WriteLock whenever a child is spawned mid-hold.

FIX: impl Drop for FileLock calling `let _ = self._file.unlock();` — flock LOCK_UN releases the lock immediately regardless of surviving OFD references in pre-exec children (fd-close still follows; error ignored, best-effort). WriteLock wraps Option<FileLock> as `_inner`, so this one Drop covers it too; the decrement-first ordering in WriteLock::drop is preserved. Rule: a rag-rat file lock must unlock explicitly on Drop — never rely on fd-close alone.

DETERMINISTIC TEST PATTERN (locks.rs tests, #[cfg(unix)], drop_releases_flock_immediately_despite_a_fork_inherited_fd): acquire a FileLock; libc::fork() a child that does NOT exec (just libc::usleep(300_000) then libc::_exit(0) — only async-signal-safe calls post-fork); parent drops the lock and immediately try_acquire the same path → asserts Some. Reap with libc::waitpid.

*** GENERALIZED CLASS (A6/PR #416 coverage incident, run 28682674819 — the SECOND instance): SAME-PROCESS-GLOBAL STATE THAT IS SAFE UNDER NEXTEST BREAKS UNDER LIBTEST. The coverage job runs plain `cargo test` under llvm-cov — every test shares ONE process with parallel libtest threads; nextest (the test job + local habit) is process-per-test and hides the whole class. Instance 2: rebuild.rs's test-only after-wave-commit barrier was a single process-global `Mutex<Option<Box<dyn Fn>>>` slot — two barrier tests racing it dropped each other's hook AND its mpsc Sender (the other test's `reached_rx.recv()` → RecvError), and a leaked hook could fire inside an UNRELATED test's rebuild. Repro model: `taskset -c 0,1 cargo test -p rag-rat-core <filter>` (5/5 deterministic pre-fix, 5/5 clean post-fix + clean full-lib rounds).

RULE: test hooks/seams in lib crates must be CONNECTION- or DATABASE-SCOPED, never process-global — key the registry by the resource the hook observes (the wave barrier: `Mutex<BTreeMap<PathBuf /*database path*/, Arc<dyn Fn + Send + Sync>>>`; production fires `run_after_wave_commit(self.database_path())`), so concurrent tests are inherently isolated (distinct temp DBs = distinct keys) and a leaked entry can't touch a stranger's run. Registration returns an RAII guard whose Drop unregisters (panic-safe — never manual cleanup a panic skips). Two mechanical notes: (a) use `Arc<dyn Fn + Send + Sync>` not Box so the dispatcher clones the hook out and RELEASES the registry lock before calling it (a hook that blocks on a test barrier must not serialize other tests' registrations); (b) mpsc endpoints are !Sync — wrap them in `Mutex` inside the hook closure to satisfy the Arc's Sync bound. VERIFY new concurrency-sensitive tests under the failing model, not just nextest: `taskset -c 0,1 cargo test -p rag-rat-core <filter>` a few rounds. (Known pre-existing flake under that model, unrelated: openai embed_batch ordering test, issue #417.) ***

title: all_symbols (edge-resolution candidate pool) must be repo-scoped — bare-open graph refresh has no scope view (PR #413 round-6)
body:
`edges::helpers::all_symbols` builds the CANDIDATE POOL for edge resolution. It joins `files` — the per-connection scope VIEW (temp.files) when one is installed (rebuild/incremental/overlay via set_context), which already filters `repo_id`. But the bare-open graph refresh path (`IndexDatabase::open` → `ensure_graph_index_current` → `resolve_edges`) installs NO scope view (set_context is not called; commit/worktree are empty), so `files` resolves to the UNSCOPED `main.files`. In a consolidated DB that pulls EVERY repo's symbols into the pool — repo A's edges resolve onto repo B's symbols, and it CRASHES ("Invalid column type Null at index 4, name value") on any sibling symbol with a NULL qualified_name.

FIX: pin the pool to the active repo with `WHERE symbols.file_id IN (SELECT id FROM main.files WHERE repo_id = ?active)` (`active` = `schema::active_repo_id(conn)`, which falls back to `sole_repo_id` when no context is installed — matching the bare-open scope). This is a NO-OP under a scope view (view rows ⊆ active repo) and the sole scope on the view-less path — so rebuild/incremental/overlay resolution is unchanged. GENERAL LESSON: a helper that reads `files` unqualified is only repo-scoped WHEN a scope view is installed; the bare `IndexDatabase::open` heal paths (ensure_graph_index_current) run WITHOUT one, so any such helper they reach needs an explicit `main.files.repo_id` predicate. Flushed by the poison-sibling harness.

*** A6 (V043) EXTENSION — the SAME lesson now has a SECOND axis, GENERATION. A full rebuild STAGES a fresh `files.generation` and leaves the superseded (dead) one in main.chunks/main.symbols/edges_data until gc, so an unqualified reader folds TWO generations. all_symbols gained `AND generation = ?` (bind `schema::active_generation(conn)` — the WRITE gen under a rebuild's scope view, the LIVE gen on the view-less bare-open heal, exactly mirroring the active_repo_id/sole_repo_id fallback) alongside the repo_id pin: `WHERE symbols.file_id IN (SELECT id FROM main.files WHERE repo_id=? AND generation=?)`. graph_index::rebuild_logical_symbols got the same `main.files.generation=?` filter. ANY raw main.chunks/main.symbols/edges_data reader that bypasses the scope view now needs BOTH the repo_id AND the generation predicate. This class flushed a REAL A6 prod bug: query/memory/validate.rs::call_path_edge_relocatable read raw `edges` (view over edges_data, no generation column of its own) with no files join, so a genuinely-deleted call site was reported `relocated` (a dead-gen edge still matched the loose from/to/kind identity) instead of `gone` until gc — fixed by `JOIN files ON files.id=edges.source_file_id`. DRIFT-TOLERATED raw readers (refresh_clone_token_df df, lexical::graph_boost ranking) were left to self-correct after gc. Full A6 design: memory mem_19f2992101e (generation-staged rebuild). ***

title: GitHub writers must upsert-RECLAIM placeholder-stranded rows — natural keys exclude repo_id (V041); V042 periphery needs no reclaim (keys lead with repo_id)
body:
THE TRAP (PR #414 P2): V041 scoped the seven github tables but deliberately kept their natural keys WITHOUT repo_id (phase-A: one repo per DB until A7) — github_refs UNIQUE(owner, repo, number, source_kind, COALESCE(source_path,''), COALESCE(source_commit,''), source_text); github_issues/github_pull_requests UNIQUE(owner, repo, number); github_ref_sync PK(owner, repo, number); comments/reviews/review_comments keyed by the github item id. The V041 consolidated-DB cardinality gate leaves pre-existing rows stranded under '__unassigned__' — and a stranded row OCCUPIES its natural key. Any conflict-IGNORING writer (`INSERT OR IGNORE`) or a DO UPDATE that omits repo_id therefore can NEVER repopulate the row: the cache is permanently stranded and invisible to scoped reads (which filter repo_id = active).

THE INVARIANT (github/store.rs header comment): every github writer RECLAIMS on conflict. store_ref: ON CONFLICT(<full 7-col expression key — the target must match the expression index EXACTLY, including the trailing source_text; omitting a column is a runtime "SQL logic error">) DO UPDATE re-stamps repo_id + refreshes ref_kind/discovered_at_ms, guarded `WHERE github_refs.repo_id != excluded.repo_id` so same-repo re-discovery keeps the old first-discovery/no-rewrite semantics. store_issue/store_pull/mark_ref_sync: `repo_id = excluded.repo_id` in their DO UPDATE SET. store_comment/store_review/store_review_comment: INSERT OR REPLACE on the id PK already reclaims (REPLACE deletes + re-inserts with the new stamp). Last-syncer-owns is the documented phase-A posture for the un-qualified keys. The github_fts mirror needs NO per-row handling: every sync path (sync_refs; sync_issue routes through it) ends in the whole-table rebuild_fts, which re-derives each mirror row's repo_id from its reclaimed base row. Test: v041_placeholder_github_rows_are_reclaimed_by_the_next_sync (repo_registry.rs) — stranded 2-repo state, one repo syncs one key, asserts re-stamp + content refresh + mirror consistency + scoped visibility + the untouched key staying placeholder.

V042 PERIPHERY AUDIT (why NO reclaim is needed there — documented at the V042 gate in migrations.rs): every post-V042 key either LEADS with repo_id (clone_token_df PK(repo_id,normalizer_kind,token_hash); clone_refinements PK(repo_id,class_key); edge_oracle PK(repo_id,tool,tool_version,source_path,bytes,edge_kind); logical_symbol_monikers PK(repo_id,logical_symbol_id,tool); dream_findings UNIQUE(repo_id,kind,subject,claim_hash)), is an append-only AUTOINCREMENT log (oracle_runs, reconcile_attempts), keys by the repo-unique generated memory id (repo_memories/bindings/tags/fts), or is a globally-unique counter (clone_graph_generations, MAX(generation)+1 across ALL repos). New writes under a real repo can never conflict with a placeholder row — stranded rows merely LINGER until a future gc sweep (memories additionally surfaced by doctor as placeholder_repo entries).

*** PR #415 UPDATE (supersedes the old "dream_findings' content-derived id (no repo fold) is NOT a blocker / A7 deferral" claim): once the dream LIFECYCLE lookups became repo-scoped (PR #415 batch 1), the repo-blind `finding_id` became a REAL error path — a reappeared claim in a second repo no longer matches the sibling's row (scoped lookup) and INSERTs the same repo-blind id into the global `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` → PK violation. `finding_id` now FOLDS repo_id (`dream::repo_folded_finding_id`, the stable_id precedent); `dream::rederive_finding_ids` re-derives persisted ids (+ remaps the in-table `superseded_by`, the only persisted reference) from the V042 apply fn and from register_repo adoption. `repo_memories.id` (`memory_id`) got the same fold (same-ms identical content across repos collided). GENERAL: scoping a subsystem's LOOKUPS around an unscoped content-derived PK converts silent cross-repo UPDATE absorption into an insert-time collision — fold the repo into the derivation in the same change that scopes the lookups. ***

GENERAL LESSON for any future "leave rows at placeholder" migration escape hatch: check whether the table's writers can actually RECLAIM the key. If the key excludes repo_id, "the next sync repopulates" is a lie without upsert-reclaim.

title: Poison-sibling tripwires need an ASSERTION on every consuming surface — seeding is detection only where a test looks
body:
PR #415 (A5 periphery review). The A5 rebase memory claimed the poison harness "flushed NO production leak". WRONG for TWELVE surfaces across two review batches — seeding was complete, but a seeded sibling row is inert until a test READs/COUNTS/CLEARS/RESOLVES against it via the exact production surface.

THE GAP: `assert_sibling_intact` only catches a mutation in a test that performs it AND asserts after; a leaky READ (count, join-by-content, "latest" ORDER BY, status header, exclusion subquery) has NO built-in tripwire — you must add a positive scoped-exclusion assertion in a test that drives that surface. THE RULE: for EACH surface consuming a scoped table, add a two-repo/poisoned test asserting isolation. Seeding is necessary, NOT sufficient. Pick seed discriminators an unscoped read would actually surface (reconcile's started_at_ms=0 seed could never win an ORDER BY DESC pick).

BATCH 1 (8): edge_oracle read+clear (edge_oracle_scope_join / clear_edge_oracle_for_tool — content join, no repo predicate); refresh_clone_token_df (unscoped symbol_fingerprints read); rebind_memory binding stamp (stranded at placeholder → stamp_bindings_from_parent_repo, from the PARENT's repo not the active one); dream lifecycle (sync_in_tx lookup/supersede/resolve/list); last_reconcile_status (global latest); resolve_moniker (scan+join+tool_has_rows probe); repo_brief memory_counts(_by_path) + orientation active_non_dir_memory_* + tree dir_memory_titles (raw readers bypassing the scoped memory API); memory_by_id (unscoped guard for get/update/mark_obsolete/rebind → cross-repo mutation by id).

BATCH 2 (4) — the REPO-BLIND DERIVED-IDENTITY class + 2 missed readers: (1) finding_id was repo-blind while dream lookups became repo-scoped → two repos minting the same (kind,subject,claim_hash) = PK VIOLATION on the global id (scoped lookup can't see the sibling row that used to absorb the UPDATE). Scoping lookups around an unscoped derived PK CREATES an error path that repo-global code didn't have. Fix: repo_folded_finding_id (stable_id precedent) + rederive_finding_ids(conn) (re-derives ids + remaps in-table superseded_by — verified the ONLY persisted finding-id reference) called from V042 apply (after backfill) AND register_repo adoption (after periphery re-point, the realign twin). (2) memory_id(now, input_hash) — same-ms identical content across repos collided; suffix now sha256(repo ‖ input_hash) when scoped; ids stay globally unique + coordination-free (phase B replication). (3) dream candidate builders: coverage_gap's repo_memory_bindings exclusion subqueries (sibling same-path binding SUPPRESSED this repo's finding — false negative) + stale_reference's repo_memories scan. (4) oracle status last_run_meta unscoped while its verdict counts were scoped — sibling's newer run headlined this repo's counts.

DERIVED-IDENTITY DISPOSITION TABLE (the phases-B+ rule: every derived identity is REPO-FOLDED, REPO-SCOPED-KEYED, or DOCUMENTED-GLOBAL — never implicit):
- REPO-FOLDED (repo in the hash): logical_symbols.id (stable_id, V040); dream_findings.id (repo_folded_finding_id); repo_memories.id (memory_id suffix).
- REPO-SCOPED KEY (repo_id in PK/UNIQUE, or keyed by a repo-unique parent): clone_refinements PK(repo_id,class_key); edge_oracle PK(repo_id,tool,ver,path,4 spans,edge_kind); logical_symbol_monikers PK(repo_id,lsid,tool); clone_token_df PK(repo_id,kind,token_hash); git_commits PK(repo_id,hash); parser_failures PK(repo_id,path); files/packages UNIQUE(repo_id,...); dream claim_hash via UNIQUE(repo_id,kind,subject,claim_hash); repo_memory_call_paths.edge_sequence_hash + bindings.binding_id (transitive via repo-unique memory_id); worktree_id (inside files' UNIQUE).
- GLOBAL BY DESIGN (documented): embedding_cache.input_hash + chunk_text_dict + name_strings (content-addressed shared pools, UNION liveness gc); chunk text/normalized/boundary hashes + symbol_fingerprints.struct_hash (freshness/pairing signals on rows transitively scoped via files — "NEVER add scope columns" note in CLONE_FINGERPRINT_DDL); clone_graph_generations.generation (global MAX+1 allocator; rows repo-stamped, clone_edges/postings transitive via the generation FK); oracle_runs/reconcile_attempts AUTOINCREMENT ids (repo-stamped logs); github (owner,repo,number)+item ids (provider-assigned, phase-A keys exclude repo → upsert-reclaim invariant, A7 widening owed); content_revision (deliberately whole-DB, V040 reclassification); repo_id itself (the scope root).
No identity is bucket-less after batch 2.

WHERE THE ASSERTIONS LANDED: oracle tests edge_oracle_reads_and_clears_are_scoped / oracle_status_header_and_counts_describe_the_active_repo; dream tests two_repos_minting_the_same_finding_do_not_collide + rederive_finding_ids_repoints; multi_repo_scope tests for rebind, moniker, dream lifecycle + candidate builders, reconcile, memory_by_id, brief+orientation+tree, clone_token_df recompute, memory_ids_fold_the_repo. Each verified non-tautological (fix reverted → test fails).

SUBTLETY: do NOT seed content-addressed tables (symbol_fingerprints) in the GLOBAL poison harness — many clone fixture tests read them whole-table as sanity counts and break. Seed such siblings per-test via two_repo_fixture instead.

title: Poison-sibling harness: distinct-path + SAME-PATH tripwire classes, resync-faithful github_fts, opt-out rules (PR #413/#414)
body:
WHAT: `crates/rag-rat-core/src/index/poison_sibling.rs` (cfg(test)). The tail of `IndexDatabase::rebuild_with_progress` calls `poison_sibling::seed_if_enabled(conn)` (default-ON per test thread). It seeds a second `poison-sibling` repo's tripwire rows into every repo-scoped table so ANY unscoped read/count/delete in production trips an EXISTING test locally instead of surfacing in review. `assert_sibling_intact(conn)` is a mutating-test post-condition (row-count + exact-sentinel-value check); call it at the end of gc/incremental/oracle/clones/memory-write tests.

TWO TRIPWIRE CLASSES (PR #414 review — the second one is load-bearing and was MISSING at first):
(1) DISTINCT-PATH rows seed under `zz_poison_`-prefixed paths/keys that never collide with a primary-repo path — they catch UNION-across-repos leaks (missing repo_id filter on a whole-table scan/delete).
(2) SAME-PATH rows seed under a REAL primary-repo path (resolved at seed time by `primary_collision_path` — lexicographically-first non-sibling `main.files.path`, fallback sentinel when the fixture indexed nothing). WHY PREFIX-ONLY SENTINELS ARE INSUFFICIENT: an aggregate that reads a scoped table grouped by a NON-repo key (path / source_path / (path,sha)) and then JOINS the result onto the active repo's rows BY THAT KEY can never see a `zz_poison_` path — the join key never matches — so join-by-non-repo-key leaks are structurally invisible to class (1). Canonical leak it flushed: repo_brief's `github_ref_counts` CTE (GROUP BY source_path, LEFT JOIN onto files by path — sibling refs on a shared path inflated github_ref_count/ranking; fixed with repo_id predicate INSIDE the CTE, A4). On A5 it flushed `validate_memories` (unscoped `FROM repo_memory_bindings` sweep that also UPDATEs anchor_status — cross-repo mutation) and `anchor_health_counts` (pooled counts); both now scoped via periphery_repo_scope_clause. SAME-PATH rows: files (sha256 sentinel), git_file_changes (additions=7700077), parser_failures (message sentinel), github_refs (number 9_900_078) at V041; repo_memory_bindings (a SECOND path-kind binding off the poison memory with the `path` COLUMN set — the distinct-path binding leaves path NULL so it never reaches `path IS NOT NULL` readers; binding_id sentinel) and edge_oracle (source_path + file_sha COLLIDE with the real primary file's sha — the edge_oracle→files join keys on path+sha; scip_symbol sentinel) at V042. Each same-path row is pinned in `sibling_tripwires` by a path-INDEPENDENT sentinel column; the pre-existing distinct-path predicates for the doubled tables were narrowed (path=…/binding_id=…/scip_symbol=…) so counts stay exactly 1. Meta-test `same_path_tripwires_expose_a_join_by_path_leak` proves liveness: an intentionally unscoped path aggregate sees the sentinel while scoped repo_brief reports 0.

GITHUB_FTS IS DERIVATION-OWNED (PR #414 P2): `github::rebuild_fts` (the sync tail) DELETEs the WHOLE mirror and re-derives one row per base-table item. The harness therefore seeds the five body-bearing base rows with EXPLICIT item ids (POISON_GH_ITEM_ID 9_900_077_000 +1..+5) and seeds FIVE mirror rows exactly as the derivation produces them (per-kind item_id/url/title/body slots; reviews url=COALESCE(html_url,'')='', review_comments title=COALESCE(path,'')=''); `classification` is recomputed by insert_fts (classify_text) and deliberately UNPINNED. Self-test `github_fts_tripwires_survive_a_papertrail_resync` calls the real rebuild_fts and asserts intact — it PINS the seed↔derivation equivalence, so a drift in either fails locally. Do NOT hand-seed a single mirror row again.

FIXTURE-FIX RULE (never weaken the harness): a test whose setup/assertion reads or mutates a scoped table by PATH without a repo predicate is a fixture bug — scope the query (has_test_code heal test, worktree-overlay scopes enumeration: `main.files WHERE path` gained `AND repo_id=?`; memory_stays_gone corruption UPDATE gained `WHERE binding_kind='symbol'` since the poison memory carries two path bindings whose ids would PK-collide). OPT-OUT (`disable_poison_sibling()`) remains ONLY for genuinely single-repo whole-DB invariants (content_revision digest, chunk_text↔chunks totals) — every opt-out is a claim, not a workaround.

V040 SHAPE (still load-bearing): the sibling is SCOPED DATA rows only — NO repos/repo_roots/repo_meta row (a registry row would hijack sole_repo_id for the many placeholder fixtures and flip multiple_real_repos). RELATED (same review): the V041/V042 backfills are cardinality-gated — on !=1 repos rows they leave rows at the placeholder instead of sole_repo_id's hard error aborting the upgrade; memory doctor surfaces placeholder-scoped repo_memories as `placeholder_repo` entries (user-authored data, unlike the refetchable github cache).

title: A4/A5 rebase onto merged A3: V041/V042 backfill P1 fix + poison periphery/github harness extension + item-8 seam-test rework
body:
Integration of the A4 (V041 github) and A5 (V042 periphery) branches onto the MERGED A3 (main d94da97, which evolved through 6 review rounds after the old A3 head the branches were authored on). End state: A4 = one V041 commit on main; A5 = A4's commit + one V042 commit. Three classes of NON-CONFLICT work the rebase required (beyond mechanical conflict resolution) — durable because the next agent merging/extending these will hit the same:

1. P1 BACKFILL FIX (V041 AND V042 — SUPERSEDES the "stamped placeholder" / "placeholder-backfilled" claims in the A4 mem_19f2517def2 and A5 mem_19f254367c4). Both migrations were authored BEFORE V039/V040 fixed the "static DEFAULT '__unassigned__' orphans rows on an already-adopted DB" class, so neither backfilled. FIX: each migration now resolves the migration-local `sole_repo_id(conn)` and re-points placeholder rows onto the real id when adopted (no-op when un-adopted — rows wait for register_repo), INSIDE the migration's own txn so it is atomic with the column-existence sentinel and only ever runs on the FIRST apply (replay-safe / consolidated-DB safe). V041: `backfill_github_repo_id_to_sole_repo` (apply_github_repo_id_scoping now self-wraps ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE...COMMIT; rebuild_github_fts_with_repo_id made TXN-LESS to run inside it) over the 7 github base tables + github_fts. V042: `backfill_periphery_repo_id_to_sole_repo` (inside the existing V042 FK-OFF txn, after rebuild_repo_memory_fts) over the 11 A5_PERIPHERY_DIRECT_SCOPED_TABLES. Tests: migration_041_backfills_an_adopted_pre_v041_db_under_the_real_repo_id, migration_042_backfills_an_adopted_pre_v042_db_under_the_real_repo_id.

2. POISON-SIBLING HARNESS EXTENSION (poison_sibling.rs). The harness is a round-6 A3 addition the branches never saw; its module doc explicitly said "when A4/A5 land, extend seed_sibling". A4 extends it with the 7 github tables + github_fts (const POISON_GH_NUMBER); A5 extends it with the V042 periphery: repo_memories(+bindings/tags(transitive, no repo_id)/fts), oracle_runs, edge_oracle, logical_symbol_monikers (the pre-existing moniker seed GAINED a repo_id column value), clone_graph_generations/clone_token_df/clone_refinements, dream_findings, reconcile_attempts (consts POISON_MEMORY_ID, POISON_GENERATION); module doc bumped V040->V041->V042 ("nothing repo-scoped left unseeded"). Extend seed_sibling + clear_sibling + sibling_tripwires TOGETHER. Running the full suite with the extended harness flushed NO production leak (A4/A5 scoping is correct); every flush was either a whole-DB-count false tripwire (opt out with `disable_poison_sibling()`: the two `*_preserves_github_papertrail_cache`, complete_generation_*/precompute_writes_graph_and_skips_when_current/refine_cache_is_read_through/unrefined_class_outside_top_n/clone_token_df_recomputed/gc_prunes_oracle_runs_for_dead_contexts) or an item-8 seam test (see #3).

3. ITEM-8 SEAM REPLACEMENT + TEST REWORK. V042 gives oracle_runs and clone_graph_generations a real repo_id, so the A3 `schema::multiple_real_repos(conn)` GUARDS (gc oracle-prune, precompute complete_generation, open_building_generation resume/discard) are REPLACED by real repo_id predicates and the guards REMOVED. Consequence: `multiple_real_repos` lost its production callers (only registry-internal resolve_config_repo_id + tests use it), so its schema::mod.rs re-export is now `#[cfg(test)]`-gated. The A3 GUARD-ERA seam TESTS (complete_generation_spares_sibling/prunes_other, open_building_spares/does_not_resume/discards_stale, gc_prunes_a_dead_oracle_run_on_a_single_repo_db, gc_skips_the_global_oracle_prune_on_a_multi_repo_db) tested the guard and BROKE: they seeded a "sibling" generation/oracle_run under the PLACEHOLDER (default) while the fixture's active repo was also placeholder (non-git clone fixture) or real (git fixture), so under the per-repo predicate the "sibling" was either treated as the active repo's own (resumed/discarded) or a placeholder run wasn't reached by a real-active prune. FIX: `seed_generation` gained an explicit `repo_id` param — "this repo's" rows seed under `&db.active_repo_id`, "sibling" rows under a distinct id ("repo-x"); the dead oracle_run is stamped `db.active_repo_id` (single-repo, so the scoped prune reaches it) or REPO_B (multi-repo, so it is spared). GENERAL LESSON: any test that constructs a "sibling repo's" periphery row MUST stamp it a repo_id distinct from `db.active_repo_id`; the placeholder default no longer suffices once the active repo is real or once the assertion depends on per-repo (not guard) semantics.

Both branches: cargo nextest run --workspace green (A4 1475, A5 1484), clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, +nightly fmt clean. Not pushed.

title: V041 GitHub papertrail + search/git-history repo_id scoping (memory-sync phase A4)
body:
A4 of the global-DB consolidation (on A1/V038, A2/V039, A3/V040). Repo-scopes the GitHub papertrail cache + closes the A3-marked search/git-history seams. LATEST 40->41; MIGRATION_041 arms added in known_version/known_migration/migration_checksum_mismatch (checksum `sha256:rag-rat-github-repo-id-scoping-v41`). FOOTGUN (cost a debug cycle, same class the A2/A3 memories flag): adding a migration to ADDITIVE_MIGRATIONS is NOT enough — `apply` runs it but `current_version` (schema::status) caps at the PREVIOUS tip until you also add the id->version arm in known_version, the `| MIGRATION_041_ID` arm in known_migration, and the checksum arm. Symptom: every migration_04x tip/forward test reports left:40 right:41.

V041 = `apply_github_repo_id_scoping` (migrations.rs). SENTINEL = `column_exists(conn,"github_fts","repo_id")`. Adds `repo_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '__unassigned__'` (REPO_ID_COLUMN_DEF) via add_column_if_missing to the 7 base tables [V041_GITHUB_SCOPED_TABLES = github_refs, github_issues, github_comments, github_pull_requests, github_reviews, github_review_comments, github_ref_sync], then REBUILDS github_fts.

*** REBASE-INTEGRATION UPDATE (A4 rebased onto MERGED A3 = main d94da97; branch head now the single V041 commit): apply_github_repo_id_scoping now SELF-WRAPS the whole migration in ONE `BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT` (the V040/V042 recipe) and `rebuild_github_fts_with_repo_id` is now TXN-LESS (runs inside the caller's txn). WHY: the P1 backfill below must be ATOMIC with the sentinel-setting FTS rebuild — else a crash after the FTS commit but before the backfill leaves the sentinel true and a re-run skips it, stranding rows under the placeholder. ***

*** P1 BACKFILL FIX (the V039/V040 class — was MISSING, added at rebase): the static `DEFAULT '__unassigned__'` stamps existing rows the placeholder, and on an ALREADY-ADOPTED DB register_repo's fast path never re-points — so scoped papertrail reads return NOTHING for the real repo until the next github sync. NEW `backfill_github_repo_id_to_sole_repo(conn)` runs INSIDE the V041 txn after the FTS rebuild: `sole_repo_id(conn)` (the migration-local resolver, hard-errors on !=1); if == LEGACY_REPO_ID it is a no-op (un-adopted — rows correctly wait for register_repo); else `UPDATE {table} SET repo_id=real WHERE repo_id=placeholder` over the 7 base tables + `github_fts`. Reached only on the FIRST apply (sentinel short-circuits replay), so `sole_repo_id`'s one-row expectation stays consistent-DB-replay safe. Test: migration_041_backfills_an_adopted_pre_v041_db_under_the_real_repo_id. THE OLD CLAIM "Rows copied stamped placeholder so papertrail survives until next sync" IS OBSOLETE — the backfill lands them under the real id immediately. ***

DELIBERATE SCOPE (the base tables gain the COLUMN only — no uniqueness-key rebuild): github_issues/github_pull_requests keep UNIQUE(owner,repo,number), github_ref_sync keeps its PK, the id-keyed caches keep their github-id PK. Phase A is ONE repo per DB (register_repo refuses a 2nd real repo until A7). Widening keys to (repo_id,owner,repo,number) is an A7 concern.

github_fts REBUILD (`rebuild_github_fts_with_repo_id`): standalone/own-content FTS5 columns can't be ALTERed, so create-new/copy/drop/rename adding `repo_id UNINDEXED` (last column). Copied rows stamped placeholder; the backfill re-points them. Leading `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS github_fts_new` = torn re-convergence.

ADOPTION: `V040_DIRECT_SCOPED_TABLES` (registry.rs) RENAMED to `DIRECT_SCOPED_ADOPTION_TABLES` and extended with the 7 github tables + github_fts (own-content FTS5 UPDATE re-points its repo_id in place). NEW: the adoption UPDATE loop is GUARDED by `adoption_table_present(conn,table)` (sqlite_master type='table'; matches FTS5 virtual tables too) — the schema-bootstrap ISOLATION fixtures seed only a subset, so an unguarded `UPDATE github_refs` would trip `no such table`. git_file_changes stays ABSENT (ON UPDATE CASCADE via git_commits). NB: the github adoption assertion can't live in the github-only ISOLATION test (adoption runs realign_logical_symbol_ids, which needs the full core schema) — it is covered by the full-schema `register_repo_repoints_github_papertrail_rows_to_the_real_id` test instead.

WRITERS stamp `crate::index::schema::active_repo_id(conn)`: store_ref/store_issue/store_comment/store_pull/store_review/store_review_comment (INSERT +repo_id), mark_ref_sync, FtsRow gained a repo_id field, insert_fts/insert_fts_rows write it, rebuild_fts SELECTs repo_id from each base table. QUERIES filter active_repo_id: evidence.rs search_fts (repo filter MANDATORY; param index TRAILS the optional item_kind bind), evidence_for_issue, evidence_for_commit_refs, refs; api.rs refs_for_path + papertrail_for_commit + status() (scoped_table_row_count per-repo); sync.rs github_ref_synced + discover_commit_refs; impact/historical.rs github_rationale_for_query (github_fts MATCH) + github_refs_for_paths (git_commits_for_paths scoping was A3's, NOT re-applied by A4).

GIT_HISTORY seams (A3-marked) closed: NEW util `scoped_table_row_count(conn,table,repo_id)`; commit_search + history_for_path filter git_commits/git_file_changes.repo_id; git_chunk_blame's wholesale DELETE replaced by `delete_repo_chunk_blame(conn,repo_id)` = delete through chunks JOIN main.files WHERE main.files.repo_id (NOT temp.files scope view). LEXICAL (search/lexical.rs): chunk_fts/chunk_embeddings scope via the files view; historical_boost/graded_git_scores take repo_id; RECALL BOUND documented at candidate_limit (8x = per-repo window).

*** POISON HARNESS EXTENDED (A4 commit): poison_sibling.rs seed_sibling/clear_sibling/sibling_tripwires now cover the 7 github tables + github_fts (const POISON_GH_NUMBER); module doc bumped V040->V041. The two `*_preserves_github_papertrail_cache` schema_migrations tests assert UNSCOPED whole-table `row_count` totals, so they `disable_poison_sibling()` (single-repo by nature). Running the full suite with the extended harness flushed NO production github leak. ***

TESTS: multi_repo_scope.rs leak matrix (seed_search_leak_data / seed_github_issue): lexical_and_hybrid / git_history_queries / papertrail_queries "never_surface_the_other_repo". repo_registry.rs owns the V041 tip pin, the github_fts rebuild+torn+adoption isolation test (seed_pre_v041_github_schema), forward-from-V040, and the two new adoption/backfill full-schema tests.

title: LocalOnly→Portable upgrade REQUIRES shallow-boundary ancestry proof (PR #413 round-6 P2 #4)
body:
Extends the identity-class decision (mem_19f271576de). A `local:` incumbent + Portable incoming is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for the in-place upgrade — `register_repo` now REQUIRES PROOF the incoming clone is a deepened version of THIS incumbent, else it refuses.

MECHANISM: `RepoIdentity` gained `shallow_boundary: Vec<String>` (sorted boundary hex for a LocalOnly id; EMPTY for Portable/pin — `resolve_repo_identity`/`derive_repo_id` populate it alongside the id, which is a hash OF exactly those bytes). At LocalOnly registration `register_repo` persists it to `repo_meta` key `shallow_boundary` (`persist_shallow_boundary`, run INSIDE the adoption txn AND on the idempotent re-registration path). At upgrade it reads the incumbent's recorded boundary (`read_shallow_boundary`) and calls `repo_identity::boundary_reachable_from_head(root, &boundary)` (gix: walk the incoming clone's HEAD ancestry, require EVERY boundary commit reachable — a `git fetch --unshallow` keeps those commits in history, an unrelated repo reaches none). Empty boundary OR unreachable OR gix error ⇒ REFUSE via `unproven_upgrade_error` (names the `[index] repo_id` pin remedy). Verified BEFORE the adoption txn so a refusal touches nothing.

WHY: a DB first indexed from a cut shallow clone, later opened from an UNRELATED full repo at the same DB path (or a mistaken pin), would otherwise silently re-point every scoped row/repo_meta/root/logical-id onto that unrelated id — data loss across two repos.

FOOTGUN: the upgrade's repo_meta re-point EXCLUDES the boundary key (`UPDATE repo_meta ... WHERE repo_id=? AND key != 'shallow_boundary'`) so it cascades away with the old `local:` repos row rather than polluting the portable id (which never upgrades). Tests: `register_repo_upgrades_a_local_only_id_to_a_portable_id_in_place` (real git, boundary=HEAD → proven), `register_repo_refuses_a_portable_upgrade_from_an_unrelated_repo`, `register_repo_refuses_a_local_upgrade_without_a_recorded_boundary`, and `unshallow_upgrades_...` end-to-end. Test helper `identity_local(id, name, boundary)` now takes the boundary vec.

title: Moving a key back to index_meta requires filtering V039's frozen relocate (else index --full hard-errors on a consolidated DB)
body:
PR #413 round-5. THE TRAP when reclassifying a V039-relocated key as GLOBAL and moving it back to index_meta (see the 18-key classification memory): V039's apply_move_per_repo_meta is FROZEN (merged) and STILL lists the key in V039_INDEX_META_KEYS. `schema::apply` (create_or_migrate / `rag-rat index --full`) RE-RUNS EVERY migration incl. V039 (only routine opens use migrate_forward = unapplied-only). So once the runtime writes the now-global key to index_meta, V039's relocate_meta_keys sees it there, its round-4 movable-keys gate fires, it resolves the migration-local sole_repo_id, and HARD-ERRORS on a consolidated (>1 real repo) DB — regressing the round-4 `full_ladder_replay_on_a_two_repo_db_is_idempotent` guard (index --full on a consolidated DB must not error).

THE FIX (migrations.rs): relocate_meta_keys now FILTERS OUT `RECLASSIFIED_GLOBAL_INDEX_META_KEYS` = [content_revision, fts_dirty, fts_source_revision, fts_synced_at_ms] before building the in_list. Those 4 are the reclassified-global keys that ALSO appear in V039_INDEX_META_KEYS; excluding them means V039's index_meta sweep no longer sees them (gate returns early, no sole_repo_id, no hard-error) while relocating every genuinely-per-repo key byte-identically. The reencode cursor is reclassified too but is NOT in this filter: it lives in V039_RECONCILE_META_KEYS and, once global, sits in index_meta where NEITHER V039 sweep names it — so it needs no exclusion; V040's move-back handles a stale repo_meta copy. This is NOT "editing V039": apply_move_per_repo_meta, the V039 key lists, and the V039 checksum (a hand-authored sentinel, not a SQL hash) are untouched; only the SHARED helper honors V040's reclassification.

THE MOVE-BACK: `move_repo_meta_keys_to_global(conn, V040_REPO_META_KEYS_TO_GLOBAL[5])` runs at the TOP of apply_repo_id_core_scoping, BEFORE the files.repo_id short-circuit (so it also fixes a DB a prior commit of this branch migrated to V040 with the keys in repo_meta). Idempotent + multi-repo-replay-safe: resolves NO sole_repo_id; INSERT OR IGNORE into the key-PK'd index_meta keeps one global value; DELETE clears every repo_meta copy; on re-apply repo_meta is empty → no-op. `value IS NOT NULL` guard skips a nullable repo_meta value (index_meta.value is NOT NULL).

TEST: v039_leaves_reclassified_global_keys_in_index_meta pins the filter; full_ladder_replay_on_a_two_repo_db_is_idempotent stays green (proves no hard-error). Test-side: any test that seeded a now-global key in repo_meta / asserted it relocated must switch to index_meta (git_history/reconcile/worktree_overlay/github_papertrail FTS tests, the v039 standalone test swapped fts_dirty→git_commit).

title: Meta-key classification: which V039-relocated keys are GLOBAL vs per-repo (V040 round-5)
body:
PR #413 round-5 (branch feat/phase-a-3-core-scoping). V039 (A2) relocated 18 singleton meta keys index_meta/reconcile_meta → repo_meta under the one-DB-per-repo assumption. 5 of them are actually GLOBAL infrastructure; V040 moves them BACK to index_meta. DO NOT re-relocate a global key in a later phase.

THE 18-KEY TABLE (key | source | class | disposition):
- source_root | index_meta | PER-REPO | stays repo_meta (this repo's config root; lifecycle open + rebuild/incremental write + query/memory/validate read)
- content_revision | index_meta | **GLOBAL** | MOVED back — `IndexDatabase::content_revision()` digests the WHOLE main.files (NO repo filter). Only writer is record_content_revision; Status.content_revision uses the METHOD (fresh), the stored key had ZERO prod readers.
- git_commit | index_meta | PER-REPO | stays (this repo's HEAD; git_meta write, query_api brief + clones/mod freshness read)
- git_dirty | index_meta | PER-REPO | stays (this repo's worktree dirty; git_meta/brief)
- graph_index_version | index_meta | PER-REPO | stays (edges are per-repo via files.repo_id; ensure_graph_index_current's DELETE was already scoped in round-3, so per-repo freshness is correct)
- active_embedding_model | index_meta | PER-REPO | stays — DECISION: each repo's rag-rat.toml names its own [llm.embedding] model; reconcile gates per-repo scope on the configured model; seed_active_embedding_model seeds per-repo from config; per-repo chunk_embeddings vectors belong to that repo's model. GLOBAL would make two repos with different embedding configs THRASH (each open reseeds the one active model, forcing the other into perpetual re-embed). (The 2 stragglers active_embedding_model_provisional + active_embedding_remote_config are moved index_meta→repo_meta by V040's existing relocate_meta_keys(V040_INDEX_META_KEYS) — same per-repo family.)
- clone_graph_live_generation | index_meta | PER-REPO | stays (pointer to THIS repo's live generation; generations are globally-unique ints, one belongs to one repo; precompute live_generation_row)
- github_last_sync_ms | index_meta | PER-REPO | stays (github/api)
- git_history_indexed_head / _root / _shallow | index_meta | PER-REPO | stay (git_history cursors)
- local_crate_roots | index_meta | PER-REPO | stays (this repo's workspace member roots; packages write, edges/imports read)
- indexed_at_ms | index_meta | PER-REPO | stays (rebuild/incremental write, brief read)
- fts_dirty / fts_source_revision / fts_synced_at_ms | index_meta | **GLOBAL** | MOVED back — chunk_fts is ONE FTS5 index over the whole chunks table (never repo-scoped) and its freshness digest is content_revision() (global). Per-repo copies caused stale-dirty loops (repo A pays a full FTS rebuild forever after repo B synced — the #219 alternating-rebuild class).
- embedding_active_model_version | reconcile_meta | PER-REPO | stays (pairs with active_embedding_model; ai/mod ACTIVE_EMBEDDING_MODEL_VERSION_META)
- vector_int8_reencode_cursor | reconcile_meta | **GLOBAL** | MOVED back — reencode.rs walks the WHOLE chunk_embeddings table (SELECT/UPDATE carry NO repo_id filter; format-only int8 conversion is repo-independent) beside an already-global done-gate (vector_int8_reencode_done stayed in index_meta). A per-repo cursor split one global walk into per-repo resume markers → a sibling open rescans from head.

NET: 5 moved back (content_revision, fts_dirty, fts_source_revision, fts_synced_at_ms, vector_int8_reencode_cursor); 13 stay. Runtime accessors for the 5 use the GLOBAL fns: fts.rs/meta.rs/query_api use self.meta/self.set_meta; reencode.rs uses ai::meta/set_meta/delete_meta (new delete_meta added to ai/helpers.rs).

title: V040 repo_id core-table scoping + active_repo_id resolver + scope-view/gc slicing (memory-sync phase A3)
body:
A3 of the global-DB consolidation (on A1/V038 + A2/V039). Scopes DIRECT core tables by repo_id, makes scope-view + gc repo-aware, replaces single_repo_id with a context resolver. LATEST 39->40; MIGRATION_040 arms in known_version/known_migration/checksum `sha256:rag-rat-repo-id-core-scoping-v40`.

V040 = `apply_repo_id_core_scoping`. DIRECT tables (repo_id NOT NULL DEFAULT '__unassigned__'): files (UNIQUE->(repo_id,path,commit_sha,worktree_id)), packages (UNIQUE->(repo_id,manifest_dir,commit_sha,worktree_id)), logical_symbols+docs (add col), parser_failures (PK->(repo_id,path), STRICT), git_commits (PK->(repo_id,hash), STRICT), git_file_changes (repo_id + composite FK ON DELETE/UPDATE CASCADE). Transitive tables scope via files.repo_id through the view.

*** BACKFILL-TARGET INVARIANT (P1): DEFAULTs are STATIC, so rebuilds stamp existing rows '__unassigned__'; on an ALREADY-ADOPTED DB register_repo's fast path never re-points -> orphan under placeholder -> EMPTY scope view after upgrade. FIX: `backfill_repo_id_to_sole_repo` runs INSIDE the V040 txn after the rebuilds (sole_repo_id, hard error on !=1). git_file_changes updated EXPLICITLY (FK OFF in the txn, so git_commits' ON UPDATE CASCADE does NOT fire). Test: migration_040_backfills_an_adopted_pre_v040_db_under_the_real_repo_id. ***

*** LOGICAL-SYMBOL KEY QUALIFICATION: `LogicalSymbolKey::stable_id(repo_id)` FOLDS repo_id (first canonical field) into the content hash so two repos with identical content derive distinct 63-bit ids. Composite PK REJECTED: `id` is the scalar `sym_<hex>` wire handle + FK/PK target of members/monikers/bindings, must stay a globally-unique scalar. Test: identical_content_in_two_repos_yields_distinct_logical_symbols. ***

*** ROUND-3 (PR #413, branch feat/phase-a-3-core-scoping) — see the sibling memory "local-only identity class + logical-symbol id realign" for the full design; key deltas: ***
1. ID-MAP REWRITE (the fold's upgrade tail): folding repo_id CHANGES every logical id the next rebuild produces, dangling pre-V040 repo_memory_bindings / repo_memory_call_paths / logical_symbol_monikers / logical_symbol_members. `graph_index.rs::realign_logical_symbol_ids(conn)` recomputes id=hash(row.repo_id ‖ key) per row (signature recovered via members->symbols; NULL-qname rows skipped) and re-points the PK + all 5 referencing columns via a NEGATIVE temp-id two-phase pass (no mid-migration PK collision). Called from V040 AFTER backfill (FK OFF) AND from register_repo adoption AFTER the placeholder->real re-point (with `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys=ON` — logical_symbol_members has an ON DELETE CASCADE FK to logical_symbols(id)). Idempotent; the two calls compose. Common upgrade (pre-V038 DB, unadopted at V040) needs BOTH: V040 aligns under the placeholder id, adoption re-aligns under the real id. Tests: migration_040_realigns_logical_symbol_ids_and_carries_bound_memories, adoption_realigns_logical_symbol_ids_so_pre_v040_memories_survive.
2. IDENTITY split corrected: a cut shallow clone is NO LONGER `Rejected` — resolve_repo_identity derives a deterministic `local:`-prefixed LocalOnly id and open_config/rebuild/incremental ADOPT it. `Rejected` now = reserved-'__unassigned__' pin + unreadable/root-less (non-shallow) history only. `Absent` (non-git/unborn HEAD) still falls back to sole_repo_id. Branch on `err.is_absent()`.
3. ensure_graph_index_current's `DELETE FROM edges_data` is now scoped (`WHERE source_file_id IN (SELECT id FROM main.files WHERE repo_id=?active)`) — a stale per-repo graph_index_version no longer wipes a sibling's edges. Test: graph_refresh_of_one_repo_leaves_the_other_repos_edges.
4. lexical::graph_boost gained a repo_id predicate (`AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM main.files f WHERE f.id=d.source_file_id AND f.repo_id=?3)`) — was the last unscoped edges_data reader; query-plan test still pins name-id index use + no files scan.
5. INCREMENTAL ADOPTION: index_incremental_with_progress now calls adopt_repo_from_config BEFORE set_context (was Self::open -> set_context, config-blind sole-repo fallback could stamp under the wrong repo on a consolidated DB). Test: incremental_adopts_the_config_repo_over_a_smaller_sibling.
6. V042 SEAMs (guarded, not scoped): oracle_runs + clone_graph_generations have NO repo_id until V042, and gc's prune_oracle_runs_outside_scope + precompute's complete_generation (`DELETE ... WHERE generation != live`) + open_building_generation (`DELETE ... WHERE status='Building'`) are GLOBAL. Guard each with `schema::multiple_real_repos(conn)` (>1 real repos): SKIP the destructive global sweep on a consolidated DB. Single-repo (every DB pre-A7) unchanged. Tests in gc/precompute + multi_repo_scope.
*** end ROUND-3 ***

RESOLVER: schema/registry.rs `active_repo_id(conn)` reads temp.connection_context['repo_id'] else `sole_repo_id`. Scope view (`write_scope_view`) filters repo_id in BOTH branches + the shadow sub-select. gc staging is repo-sliced; SHARED content-addressed tables (name_strings, embedding_cache, chunk_text_dict) stay GLOBAL with UNION liveness.

FOOTGUN: V008's files rebuild drops repo_id on every apply() (schema::apply re-runs EVERY migration). Guard with `files_has_commit_scoped_unique(conn)`.

OPEN-FLOW: open_config/rebuild/incremental: open -> adopt_repo_from_config -> set_context -> manifest heal. Registration MUST precede the manifest heal. bare open() uses sole_repo_id; try_open_config_read_only NOW uses resolve_config_repo_id (see ROUND-4).

TESTS: multi_repo_scope.rs two_repo_fixture (indexes A for real, seeds B directly). repo_registry.rs owns the V040 tip pin, backfill, torn-state/FK-CASCADE adoption, the id-realign tests, and the open_config error-class pins (reserved pin surfaces; shallow ADOPTS under LocalOnly; non-git falls back). HANDOFF A4=github(V041); A5=periphery(V042); A6=scope-view generation filter.

*** ROUND-4 (PR #413) READ-PATH SCOPING + MULTI-REPO REPLAY IDEMPOTENCE (findings #1/#2/#3): (a) NEW schema::resolve_config_repo_id(conn, root, override) -> Option<String> (registry.rs) is the READ-path counterpart to register_repo (registers NOTHING): route1 = derive identity, use it IF it is a registered real repo; route2 = the recorded repo_roots mapping for the root (override-independent, catches pinned/local/portable); route3 = sole repo on a single-repo DB, else None on a consolidated one. A Rejected pin -> None (surfaces via the read-write open). try_open_config_read_only now uses it (NOT sole_repo_id) AND builds the db + set_context BEFORE the manifest/embedding-seed gates, so those gates' internal active_repo_id resolves to the CONFIG repo — previously they ran context-less and hit sole_repo_id -> a SIBLING in a consolidated DB, falsely reporting heal-owed (returned None). (b) install_worktree_scope_view now takes an EXPLICIT repo_id arg; the raw-conn callers (CLI + MCP grep-augment hooks, query::orientation) resolve it via index::resolve_scope_repo_id(conn, config_root, override) and pass it (empty string = sibling-safe empty scope). The old active_repo_id-fallback helper install_scope_view is now #[cfg(test)]-only. (c) FINDING-3: relocate_meta_keys gained an IDEMPOTENCE GATE (SELECT EXISTS ... key IN (...)) BEFORE its migration-local sole_repo_id — on a re-apply the source keys are already moved, so it returns early WITHOUT resolving sole_repo_id. That is what makes schema::apply (create_or_migrate / index --full) stop HARD-ERRORING at V039 on a consolidated >1-repo DB. V038 (NOT-EXISTS seed guard) and V040 (files.repo_id sentinel short-circuit) were already replay-safe — proven by full_ladder_replay_on_a_two_repo_db_is_idempotent (replays the WHOLE ladder on a 2-repo DB, asserts no error + no data movement, on a FRESH conn since the fixture conn carries the temp.files view). Read-path tests: read_only_open_binds_the_config_repo_over_a_smaller_sibling, resolve_config_repo_id_binds_a_recorded_root_over_the_sole_pick, resolve_config_repo_id_returns_none_for_a_rejected_pin. ***

title: V038 repos registry + register_repo adoption contract (memory-sync phase A1)
body:
A1 of the global-DB consolidation. Adds V038 (`repos`/`repo_roots`/`repo_meta`, all STRICT) + `repo_identity.rs` + `data_dir.rs` + a parse-only `[index] repo_id` config override. NO scoping of other tables and NO default-path flip yet (those are A3 / A7).

REGISTRY SHAPE (schema/migrations.rs `apply_repos_registry` / `REPOS_REGISTRY_DDL`). `repos(repo_id PK, display_name, registered_at_ms)`; `repo_roots(repo_id FK->repos ON DELETE CASCADE, root, registered_at_ms, PK(repo_id,root))`; `repo_meta(repo_id FK->repos ON DELETE CASCADE, key, value, PK(repo_id,key))`. Seeds ONE placeholder row repo_id='__unassigned__'; that literal MUST equal schema::LEGACY_REPO_ID. CASCADE FKs point at repos (not a REINDEX_VOLATILE_PARENT), so the volatile-FK trip-wire does NOT flag them.

PLACEHOLDER-SEED INVARIANT (was a real bug). The seed is CONDITIONAL: INSERT OR IGNORE ... SELECT '__unassigned__','',0 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM repos WHERE repo_id != '__unassigned__'). WHY: schema::apply re-runs EVERY additive migration, and IndexDatabase::rebuild reaches it via create_or_migrate on an ALREADY-ADOPTED DB. After adoption removed the placeholder, a plain INSERT OR IGNORE re-mints it beside the real row (test reapplying_schema_after_adoption_does_not_resurrect_the_placeholder). Any NEW state a migration seeds that adoption later removes MUST carry the same "only when un-adopted" guard.

register_repo (schema/registry.rs, pub fn register_repo(conn, &RepoIdentity, root, now_ms) -> rusqlite::Result<String>). Idempotent, called on every open. Cases: (1) repo_id already the real id → no-op except INSERT OR IGNORE root into repo_roots. (2) NO real id yet (only placeholder) → ADOPTION (inside ONE txn): INSERT the real repos row, re-point repo_meta children, re-point the V040 direct-scoped tables, realign logical-symbol ids (see A3 EXTENSION), DELETE the placeholder repos row, record root. (3) a DIFFERENT real repo_id already owns the DB → REFUSE (SQLITE_CONSTRAINT) — the single-repo invariant for phase A; A7 turns register_repo into multi-repo registration. (ROUND-4: case (3) now has ONE exception — a `local:` incumbent + a Portable incoming UPGRADES; see the ROUND-4 block below.)

A3 ADOPTION EXTENSION (V040, mem_19f24ea3aac). Inside the SAME adoption txn, after the repo_meta UPDATE and before the placeholder DELETE, register_repo loops `V040_DIRECT_SCOPED_TABLES` = [files, packages, logical_symbols, docs, parser_failures, git_commits] running `UPDATE {table} SET repo_id=real WHERE repo_id=placeholder`. git_file_changes is DELIBERATELY ABSENT (its (repo_id,commit_hash) FK is ON UPDATE CASCADE, carried by the git_commits rewrite). repo_meta handled by the earlier UPDATE.

*** ROUND-3 (PR #413): the adoption loop is followed by `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys=ON` + `graph_index.rs::realign_logical_symbol_ids(&tx)`. WHY: re-pointing logical_symbols.repo_id changes the id every row SHOULD have (stable_id folds repo_id, A3), so the next rebuild_logical_symbols would dangle every pre-adoption repo_memory_bindings / repo_memory_call_paths / logical_symbol_monikers / logical_symbol_members handle. realign recomputes id=hash(real ‖ key) and re-points the PK + all 5 referencing columns IN PLACE. It must run with FK checks DEFERRED because logical_symbol_members has an ON DELETE CASCADE FK to logical_symbols(id) and adoption runs foreign_keys=ON — an immediate parent-id UPDATE would trip the child FK; defer_foreign_keys=ON auto-resets at commit. Idempotent with V040's own realign (the two compose for the pre-V038-upgrade path). Test: adoption_realigns_logical_symbol_ids_so_pre_v040_memories_survive. ***

RESERVED-ID GUARD (defense in depth). register_repo ALSO refuses UP FRONT any identity.repo_id.trim() that is EMPTY/whitespace OR == LEGACY_REPO_ID (a caller can hand-build a RepoIdentity; registering the placeholder degenerates adoption). Tests: register_repo_refuses_the_reserved_placeholder_and_stays_adoptable; register_repo_refuses_an_empty_or_whitespace_repo_id.

repo_identity.rs (resolve_repo_identity(root, override_id)). Default repo_id = LEXICOGRAPHICALLY SMALLEST root-commit hash reachable from HEAD (a Portable id). A trimmed non-empty override wins (Portable) EXCEPT __unassigned__/LEGACY_REPO_ID, which is REFUSED. display_name = working-tree dir name. *** SHALLOW POSTURE UPDATED (PR #413): a cut shallow clone (no reachable parentless root) NO LONGER errors — it derives a DETERMINISTIC `local:`-prefixed LocalOnly id from the sorted `.git/shallow` boundary (via repo.shallow_commits()), logs ONE warning, and proceeds. Identity now carries `class: RepoIdentityClass{Portable|LocalOnly}`. RepoIdentityError shrank: `Rejected` = reserved pin + unreadable/root-less (non-shallow) history only; `Absent` = non-git/unborn HEAD (adopt_repo_from_config falls back to sole_repo_id). See the sibling identity-class memory bound to repo_identity.rs. *** Unborn HEAD → empty_repo_error (Absent). Config gained parse-only pub repo_id_override; adopt_repo_from_config passes it into resolve_repo_identity.

data_dir.rs — global_database_path() = data_dir()/rag-rat.sqlite via XDG cascade. Not wired into path resolution yet (A7).

A2 REVIEW-FIX — ADOPTION IS ATOMIC: register_repo wraps the WHOLE adoption in ONE conn.unchecked_transaction() (INSERT real repos row / UPDATE repo_meta / UPDATE the V040 tables / realign / DELETE placeholder / record_repo_root / commit). WAS A REAL BUG: separate autocommits left a torn state (both real row AND placeholder) the case-(1) fast path never repairs. Test register_repo_adoption_is_atomic_on_a_mid_sequence_failure. V039's relocate_meta_keys resolves a migration-local sole_repo_id (hard error on !=1). NB the LADDER does NOT wrap apply fns in a txn — a non-idempotent multi-statement migration self-wraps (V040's rebuilds do).

*** ROUND-4 (PR #413): register_repo GAINS the LocalOnly->Portable UPGRADE transition. Case order now: (1) real_ids contains incoming id -> no-op + record root; (2) real_ids == [local:X] AND incoming identity.class==Portable -> UPGRADE; (3) any OTHER different real id -> REFUSE (Portable vs diff-Portable; a LocalOnly incoming vs a real incumbent — a deepened clone must NOT downgrade a portable id). The adoption txn is generalized: repoint_from = upgrade_from (the local id) .or(placeholder_present ? LEGACY_REPO_ID). It re-points repo_meta + V040_DIRECT_SCOPED_TABLES + repo_roots (NEW: the local id has recorded roots and repo_roots FK is ON DELETE CASCADE, so move them BEFORE deleting the source repos row; the placeholder never has roots so the UPDATE is a no-op there) FROM source_id, then PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys=ON + realign_logical_symbol_ids + DELETE the source repos row. A tracing::warn! on the upgrade path states the local->portable re-point. Guarded on exactly one real repo (a consolidated DB is never upgraded here). Tests (repo_registry.rs): register_repo_upgrades_a_local_only_id_to_a_portable_id_in_place (files+roots re-pointed, bound memory survives the realign, local id gone), register_repo_refuses_a_local_only_incoming_against_a_real_incumbent, register_repo_refuses_a_portable_incoming_against_a_portable_incumbent, and end-to-end unshallow_upgrades_a_shallow_clone_index_from_local_to_portable_in_place. A pinned `local:` id is refused by resolve_repo_identity (see the identity-class memory). ***

title: Repo identity portability class: Portable vs LocalOnly (open-time never hard-rejects a shallow clone)
body:
PR #413 (branch feat/phase-a-3-core-scoping). `resolve_repo_identity(root, override_id) -> Result<RepoIdentity, RepoIdentityError>` in crates/rag-rat-core/src/repo_identity.rs. `RepoIdentity` gained `class: RepoIdentityClass { Portable | LocalOnly }` (scoping-neutral tag, never an identity input, not persisted).

WHY THIS EXISTS: the CI benchmark/eval/oracle jobs index fixture corpora from SHALLOW checkouts (--depth 1). The prior A3 code REJECTED a cut shallow clone (`RepoIdentityError::Rejected`, "cannot derive a stable repo_id from the shallow clone…"), and that error PROPAGATED through open_config/rebuild -> every one of those CI jobs panicked (runs 28630900729/712/713). Blocking indexing on a shallow checkout is wrong: the id IS stable on this machine, it just isn't portable across machines.

THE RULE — open-time resolution MUST NOT hard-reject a shallow clone; it downgrades the class instead:
- Full history reachable (a parentless root commit) -> `Portable`, id = lexicographically-smallest root-commit hash (unchanged).
- Explicit `[index] repo_id` pin (non-reserved) -> `Portable` (the user chose a stable string).
- Cut shallow clone (NO reachable parentless root) -> `LocalOnly`, id = `local:<sha256 hex of the sorted .git/shallow boundary commit hashes>`, via `repo.shallow_commits()` (gix keeps that list SORTED, so two opens of the SAME clone hash identical bytes → deterministic; a DEEPER clone has a different boundary → a different id, which is exactly why it is not portable). Logs ONE `tracing::warn!` naming the future constraint + both remedies (`git fetch --unshallow`, or pin `[index] repo_id`), then PROCEEDS. register_repo adopts the `local:` id as a normal real repo.

`RepoIdentityError` SHRANK to genuinely-invalid inputs: `Rejected` = a reserved-'__unassigned__' pin OR an unreadable/root-less (NON-shallow) history (walk failure / corrupt graph). `Absent` (unchanged) = not a git repo / unborn HEAD → adopt_repo_from_config falls back to sole_repo_id (single-repo/unadopted, pre-A3 behavior). Callers branch on `err.is_absent()`; a shallow clone is now an `Ok(LocalOnly)`, never an error.

WHERE THE HARD GATE LIVES INSTEAD: not at open/index time — in the future family-sync layer, which will refuse to replicate a non-Portable id (a LocalOnly id would split a repo's identity across machines). `class` travels with the identity so sync can enforce that; indexing never does.

TESTS (repo_identity.rs unit + repo_registry.rs integration): shallow_clone_that_cuts_history_gets_a_deterministic_local_only_id (asserts LocalOnly, `local:` prefix, determinism across two opens, pin overrides to Portable); shallow_clone_covering_full_history_resolves_the_real_root (a depth-covering shallow clone is Portable — `is_shallow()` alone would wrongly downgrade it; the "no reachable parentless root" signal is what distinguishes cut-vs-covered); open_config_adopts_a_shallow_clone_under_a_local_only_id; git_history_reload_is_not_skipped_on_a_shallow_clone now runs UNPINNED (exercises the LocalOnly adoption path the CI fixtures hit).

APPLY: don't reintroduce a shallow-clone rejection at open/index time. If you need "portable identity required," check `class == Portable` at the sync boundary, not in resolve_repo_identity. See the V038 adoption memory (mem_19f2433a36c) and V040 memory (mem_19f24ea3aac) for how the id then flows through registration/scoping.

*** ROUND-4 (PR #413, branch feat/phase-a-3-core-scoping): `LOCAL_ONLY_ID_PREFIX = "local:"` is now a SHARED `pub const` in repo_identity.rs (used by local_only_id_from_boundary AND register_repo). resolve_repo_identity now REFUSES a pinned override that starts with `local:` (Rejected class, reserved_local_prefix_error) — the prefix is reserved for machine-derived shallow ids, and register_repo keys its LocalOnly->Portable UPGRADE off an incumbent id carrying it, so a pinned `local:` id would be ambiguous. A cut shallow clone that is later deepened (`git fetch --unshallow`) resolves Portable again; register_repo then re-points the existing index from the local: id to the portable one IN PLACE (see the V038 adoption memory) instead of the old dead-end refusal. Test: override_with_the_reserved_local_prefix_is_refused. ***

title: V042 clone/oracle/reconcile/memory periphery repo_id scoping + integration onto V041 (memory-sync phase A5)
body:
A5 of the global-DB consolidation (on A1/V038, A2/V039, A3/V040, A4/V041). Scopes the DIRECT periphery tables the A3/A4 sweeps left GLOBAL. LATEST 41->42; MIGRATION_042 arms in known_version/known_migration/migration_checksum_mismatch (checksum `sha256:rag-rat-repo-id-periphery-scoping-v42`) — the same "arms not enough / add all three or current_version caps at prior tip" footgun the A2-A4 memories flag.

V042 = `apply_repo_id_periphery_scoping` (migrations.rs). SENTINEL = `column_exists(conn,"repo_memories","repo_id")` (all-or-nothing; the whole migration is ONE self-wrapped `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF; BEGIN IMMEDIATE;…COMMIT; foreign_keys=ON` because the ladder runs apply fns in AUTOCOMMIT — the V040 recipe). Each rebuild starts `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS <t>_new` for torn-state re-convergence. THREE shapes:
- ADDITIVE column (`A5_ADDITIVE_SCOPED_TABLES`, add_column_if_missing REPO_ID_COLUMN_DEF): clone_graph_generations, oracle_runs, reconcile_attempts, repo_memories, repo_memory_bindings.
- KEY REBUILD (repo_id joins the PK/UNIQUE → table rebuild): clone_token_df PK(repo_id,normalizer_kind,token_hash); clone_refinements PK(repo_id,class_key); edge_oracle content-key PK prepends repo_id (+3 idx); logical_symbol_monikers PK(repo_id,logical_symbol_id,tool) (+1 idx); dream_findings UNIQUE(repo_id,kind,subject,claim_hash) (+2 idx). STRICT preserved.
- STANDALONE FTS: repo_memory_fts DROP+CREATE with `repo_id UNINDEXED`, repopulated from repo_memories (so repo_id comes from each memory's freshly-added column; group_concat reads repo_memory_tags).
clone_edges/clone_subblock_postings are NOT scoped — the clone GENERATION integer stays GLOBALLY unique (allocated MAX(generation)+1 over ALL repos), so a build_generation belongs to exactly one repo and those children scope transitively; only the generation SWEEPS (complete_generation, Building cleanup, postings invalidation) got a repo_id predicate so a repo's precompute never deletes a sibling's gens. symbol_fingerprints/symbol_token_postings stay symbol_id-keyed (transitive via symbols->files.repo_id) — the CLONE_FINGERPRINT_DDL "never add scope columns" rule is about the COMMIT/WORKTREE axis; repo_id is a different cross-repo axis and only clone_token_df/clone_refinements there take it.

GATING (schema/registry.rs `periphery_repo_scope(conn, probe_table) -> Option<String>` + `periphery_repo_scope_clause(&Option<String>, qualifier)`): every periphery query sweep gates its repo_id predicate on the probe — Some(active_repo_id) when the column is present (a normal open runs the full ladder incl. V042), None on a raw connection that never ran the ladder (→ original unscoped SQL). Reads interpolate an escaped-literal ` AND t.repo_id='…'` (NOT a bind param — these carry positional/`IN(...)` lists; the id is registry-validated content, quotes doubled); writers embed the id as a per-call literal prefix so bound params + ON-CONFLICT targets are the only thing that changes when scoped. The rebuilt PKs force write_edge_oracle / write_logical_symbol_moniker / the df bump / clone_refinements INSERT-OR-REPLACE to WIDEN their ON CONFLICT target in the scoped branch. Sweeps touched: query/memory (create stamp; memory_search, memories_for_*, list_memories, doctor_* filter repo_id; duplicate_memory_id +repo_id so dedupe never crosses repos; upsert_memory_fts writes repo_id; moniker_for_logical_symbol* filter); clones (precompute generation sweeps, substrate/of_text df reads, refine/cache read+write, file_index df bump, rebuild refresh_clone_token_df); oracle/store (oracle_runs record/read/prune, edge_oracle write/clear/prune, monikers count/clear/write).

ADOPTION: `A5_PERIPHERY_DIRECT_SCOPED_TABLES` (registry.rs, the 5 additive + 5 rebuilt + repo_memory_fts) re-pointed in register_repo's adoption txn, each guarded by `column_exists(tx, table, "repo_id")`. This is a STRONGER guard than A4's `adoption_table_present` (table-existence) and it MUST be: several periphery tables (dream_findings, edge_oracle, clone_token_df, logical_symbol_monikers, oracle_runs) predate V042 and exist at earlier schema versions WITHOUT the column, so a partial-schema fixture that stopped before V042 has the table but not the column.

DEFERRED (schema column + adoption done, QUERY scoping not): dream_findings + reconcile_attempts writers use no ON CONFLICT so they don't break on the scoped schema — they operate on the '__unassigned__' partition, single-repo-correct for phase A; multi-repo dream/reconcile isn't reachable until A7. edge_oracle metric READS (edge_oracle_scope_join, clear_edge_oracle_for_tool) stay transitively scoped via their files join (the WRITE stamps repo_id); only a cross-repo path+sha256 collision could leak.

INTEGRATION (this A5 branch = A4's V041 commit + ONE A5 commit). A5 was authored UNREGISTERED (a sibling owned V041) then registered here: purely additive (consts + LATEST bump + ADDITIVE_MIGRATIONS entry after V041 + the 3 recognizer arms + drop the `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]` off the apply fn/6 rebuild helpers/A5_ADDITIVE_SCOPED_TABLES). Rebase conflicts (both stacked on A3/627e8d8): migrations.rs — A4's V041 fns and A5's V042 block both insert after rebuild_git_commits_tables_with_repo_id and git aligned their trailing braces; resolve by co-locating BOTH (additive) and inserting the missing `}` for rebuild_github_fts_with_repo_id between them. multi_repo_scope.rs — both APPEND-ONLY (single `@@ -180` hunk each), A5 namespaces its helpers a5_/A5_ so no collision; reconstruct = A4's full file + A5's block (lines 183+). registry.rs/mod.rs auto-merged (A4 renamed V040_DIRECT_SCOPED_TABLES->DIRECT_SCOPED_ADOPTION_TABLES; A5 added its own const/loop after).

TESTS: repo_registry.rs owns the migration-shape coverage (A4's placement convention). migration_042_is_the_latest_tip_and_scopes_periphery owns the absolute LATEST==42 pin (V041's tip test dropped to symbolic — "pin moves to the new tip"). migration_042_periphery_rebuild_preserves_rows_and_reconverges_from_torn_state is the DIRECT-FN ISOLATION test: builds the pre-V042 schema via `seed_pre_v042_periphery_schema` = calling the real pub(crate) DDL fns (apply_baseline + apply_oracle_tables + apply_scip_moniker_anchors + apply_clone_fingerprint_tables + apply_clone_graph_tables + apply_dream_findings + apply_repos_registry) — DRIFT-PROOF vs hand-copied CREATE TABLEs (per the "assert deferred-absence against the migration DDL in isolation" Risk memory). FOOTGUN: that isolation test must NOT call register_repo — apply_baseline creates `files` WITHOUT repo_id (V040 not run in a periphery-only fixture), so adoption's DIRECT_SCOPED_ADOPTION_TABLES loop (table-presence guard) would `UPDATE files SET repo_id` → "no such column". Adoption is instead covered by full_ladder_v037_to_v042_scopes_both_workstreams_data (full schema): seed A4 (github) + A5 (memory/oracle/clone) rows under the placeholder, truncate_schema_to(37), migrate_forward re-runs the WHOLE A-phase (safe: V038 INSERT OR IGNORE...WHERE NOT EXISTS + V039 copy-before-delete are idempotent, V040/V041/V042 sentinel-short-circuit), assert rows intact under the placeholder, then ONE register_repo re-points BOTH workstreams' rows to the real id. The multi_repo_scope A5 tests were converted from direct-fn to the LADDER (drop the explicit apply_repo_id_periphery_scoping call — schema::apply now runs V042; the clone_precompute test's DROP-VIEW-then-apply workaround is gone because V042 runs at open BEFORE install_scope_view).

Gates: cargo nextest run --workspace 1445 passed; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; +nightly fmt clean (the struct_lit_style warnings are pre-existing rustfmt.toml config noise). HANDOFF A6: generation-staged rebuild adds files.generation; the scope view's write_scope_view gains `AND files.generation=<live>`. A7: register_repo becomes multi-repo (drops the single-repo refusal); the deferred dream_findings/reconcile_attempts query scoping + the github uniqueness-key widening land then.

title: V039 per-repo meta relocation + single_repo_id stand-in (memory-sync phase A2)
body:
A2 of the global-DB consolidation (stacked on A1/V038). Moves the per-repo SINGLETON meta keys out of global `index_meta`/`reconcile_meta` into `repo_meta` under the `LEGACY_REPO_ID` ('__unassigned__') placeholder, and threads every read/write through a repo-scoped path. No other table scoped (A3+); reconcile_meta TABLE deliberately NOT dropped (later cleanup).

V039 = `apply_move_per_repo_meta` (registered in ADDITIVE_MIGRATIONS; LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION 38->39; MIGRATION_039 arms in known_version/known_migration/migration_checksum_mismatch; checksum `sha256:rag-rat-per-repo-meta-v39` is a hand-authored sentinel, nothing hashes the SQL). `relocate_meta_keys` does copy-then-delete per source table (INSERT OR IGNORE on the (repo_id,key) PK + DELETE), idempotent + torn-run-safe. MOVED index_meta keys: source_root, content_revision, git_commit, git_dirty, graph_index_version, active_embedding_model, clone_graph_live_generation, github_last_sync_ms, git_history_indexed_{head,root,shallow}, local_crate_roots, indexed_at_ms, fts_{dirty,source_revision,synced_at_ms}. MOVED reconcile_meta keys: embedding_active_model_version, vector_int8_reencode_cursor. STAYED GLOBAL (machine-level or postdate the plan inventory): generated_flags_version, the reencode DONE gate, throughput-tune cache, and the active-model provenance siblings below.

ACCESSORS. meta.rs primitives `pub(crate) repo_meta/set_repo_meta/set_repo_meta_if_changed/delete_repo_meta(conn, repo_id, key[, value]) -> rusqlite::Result` (delete_repo_meta added beyond the plan's 3 — clear paths need it). Re-exported at crate::index scope. IndexDatabase METHOD wrappers (same names, `self.repo_meta(key)`) resolve the repo + call the primitives (self.-style sites: fts, git_meta, graph_index, packages, incremental, rebuild, query_api/mod, clones/mod+precompute:408, record_content_revision). AI-module 2-arg wrappers in ai/helpers.rs mirror the ai::meta/set_meta/delete_meta trio.

single_repo_id(conn) (schema/registry.rs, re-exported schema::single_repo_id) = the connection-level ACTIVE-REPO STAND-IN until A3. Returns the SOLE `repos` row (placeholder before adoption — the A2 common case since register_repo is NOT yet wired into open_config; real id after). debug_assert = exactly ONE repos row (NOT "non-placeholder": a legacy un-adopted DB's only row IS the placeholder). A3 REPLACES every single_repo_id(conn) with context.repo_id.
