Free-conn threading sites A3 must convert: git_history apply_prepared/status/is_history_current/clear; github/api sync_from_refs/sync_issue/status; precompute live_generation_row; edges/imports load_local_roots; query/memory/validate persisted_source_root; ai reconcile (helpers active_embedding_model_id/_version, model_lifecycle activate/clear/seed_owed/is_missing, manifest model_manifest_is_current/remove_legacy_models raw SQL, reencode load/save/clear_cursor); lifecycle open paths (source_root x2, graph_index_version). The IndexDatabase wrappers resolve it internally (A3 edits the wrapper body once).

register_repo ADOPTION EXTENDED (Step 4): INSERT real repos row FIRST, `UPDATE repo_meta SET repo_id=real WHERE repo_id=placeholder`, then DELETE the placeholder repos row. Insert-first/delete-last keeps the enforced FK (repo_meta -> repos, foreign_keys=ON at storage.rs:136, no ON UPDATE CASCADE) satisfied at each statement boundary without a txn/deferred checks — an in-place UPDATE of repos.repo_id would violate the FK once repo_meta has placeholder children. repo_roots never has placeholder rows (record_repo_root only writes under a real id). A3 extends re-pointing to its new direct-scoped tables. title: Active embedding model is seeded from config on a fresh index — it does NOT default to embedding-hash (#394)
body:
BUG (#394) + fix. `active_embedding_model_id(conn)` (index/ai/helpers.rs) falls back to `HASH_MODEL_ID` when the `active_embedding_model` meta is UNSET, and nothing seeded it from config — so a fresh index silently used `embedding-hash` regardless of `[llm.embedding] model`, and `reconcile` blocked naming `embedding-hash` instead of the configured model. `EmbeddingBackend::default()` is all-MiniLM, NEVER hash.

FIX: `seed_active_embedding_model(conn, configured_model_id)` (index/ai/reconcile/model_lifecycle.rs) activates `config.llm.embedding.backend.model_id()` when a seed is owed. Called from every config-aware open: `rebuild` + `index_incremental_with_progress` (both INSIDE their txn — see atomicity), `open_config`, and `try_open_config_read_only` (returns None when a seed is owed → read-only tools fall back to the healing write path).

SEED-OWED = PROVENANCE, NOT A PROXY (load-bearing lesson). Don't infer "was the active model a user choice?" from `ai_models.installed` (a recovered cache is installed too) or `current_embedding_count` (explicit install has 0 embeddings pre-reconcile, AND it's an O(index) scan every open). RECORD it: `ACTIVE_EMBEDDING_MODEL_PROVISIONAL_META` ("active_embedding_model_provisional") = "1" AUTOMATIC / "0" or absent EXPLICIT|CONFIRMED. `activate_model_with_version(conn, id, version, provisional)` is the SINGLE writer stamping model+version+provenance together — `install_model` false (explicit), `recover_cached_fastembed_model` + the seed true (automatic). A reconcile committing embeddings (`embed_loop.rs`, `report.embeddings_written > 0`) calls `clear_active_embedding_model_provisional` → confirmed. `active_embedding_model_seed_owed`: model selected ⇒ owed when active unset OR (active != config AND `active_embedding_model_is_provisional`) — O(1). Absent flag ⇒ non-provisional ⇒ respected (pre-#394 indexes + explicit/committed models safe). One signal: explicit install sticks before first reconcile; recovered cache yields to config; config edit before install adopted; committed model never clobbered; no per-open scan.

EMBEDDINGS-OFF SYMMETRY (config `model="none"`, model_id()==None): reconcile/status are config-BLIND (`reconcile_with_options_progress`/`status.rs` read `active_embedding_model_id` from the active meta, NOT config; the CLI reconcile cmd does NOT gate on config=None), so the SEED is the ONLY config→meta bridge — disabling must flow through it too. `seed_owed(None)` owes a write only to CLEAR a still-active PROVISIONAL model (explicit/confirmed preserved) → `clear_active_embedding_model` drops model id + freshness version + provenance flag + remote config, so `active_embedding_model_id` returns to the hash fallback and nothing stale lingers. Restores the "embeddings-off ⇒ active unset" invariant; without it a repo first opened with a real embedder then switched to `none` keeps prompting for the disabled model. `delete_meta` is the index_meta counterpart of `clear_reconcile_meta` (`clear_active_remote_config` now builds on it).

TWO GAPS THE SEED SHARED WITH install (fix both when touching activation): (1) the seed clears `active_remote_config` (like `install_model`'s local branch) — else a reseed away from a remote activation lets `active_embedder` build an `OpenAiEmbedder` against the STALE endpoint → vectors in the wrong embedding space. (2) ATOMICITY — BOTH write-path seeds run INSIDE their transaction, never autocommit-before-BEGIN (a failed pass would otherwise strand the active model on a newly configured MISSING model, losing the old fallback): the `rebuild` seed before COMMIT (after set_meta indexed_at_ms); the `index_incremental_with_progress` seed inside its BEGIN IMMEDIATE block, folded into the `mutated` flag so a heal COMMITs while an idle pass with no heal owed stays a no-op read (preserves the #63 no-write invariant).

Seeding does NOT install — reconcile still BLOCKS until the configured model is installed — but the block message (`embed_loop.rs` / `status.rs`) names the CONFIGURED model.

TEST FOOTGUN: schema_bootstrap tests use `embedding-hash` as the no-download test embedder and used to rely on active-defaults-to-hash. A fresh index now adopts the CONFIGURED model, so a test that installs/uses hash must SELECT it (`config.llm.embedding.backend = HASH_MODEL_ID.parse().unwrap()` before `rebuild`): fixed `reconcile_requires_explicit_model_install_and_ignores_stale_artifacts`, `full_rebuild_preserves_installed_model_manifest`. Provenance unit tests (in-memory conn): respects_an_explicitly_installed_model, config_wins_over_a_provisionally_recovered_model, reseeds_a_provisional_model_when_the_config_changes, a_confirmed_model_is_respected_over_a_config_change, embeddings_off_clears_a_provisional_active_model, embeddings_off_preserves_an_explicit_active_model, embeddings_off_leaves_the_active_model_unset. Integration: reconcile_confirms_a_provisional_model_against_a_config_change; an_incremental_pass_heals_a_missing_active_model_atomically. `activate_model_with_version_writes_all_metas` asserts the provenance meta. PR #395.

title: files.generated unifies "generated" across the query layer; kind=generated files have NO symbols, path-heuristic codegen does (#202)
body:
Two distinct "generated" mechanisms in the indexer, and #202 unified them:

1. **`files.kind = 'generated'`** (target classification, from the rag-rat.toml target's `TargetKind`). A `kind=generated` file is **chunk-only — it gets NO symbols** (`prep.rs`/`file_index.rs`: symbol extraction is gated `kind != Generated`). So a correctly-classified generated target can never pollute symbol search — nothing in `symbols` to match.

2. **`files.generated` (INTEGER column)** — the flag the QUERY layer filters on. Search (`search/lexical.rs`), orientation, tree, clusters, and symbol search all default to `files.generated = 0` with an `include_generated` opt-in. BEFORE #202 it was set purely from `matches!(kind, Generated)`.

THE BUG (#202): codegen living UNDER a source target — e.g. ubrn FFI bindings at `packages/.../src/generated/*.ts`, indexed by a plain source binding — keeps `kind = source`, gets FULL symbol extraction, and had `generated = 0`. So it polluted symbol_lookup AND search, and a `kind != 'generated'` filter could never catch it.

THE FIX: `crate::index::file_is_generated(kind, path) = matches!(kind, Generated) || is_generated_path(path)` feeds the `generated` column at both insert sites. Those files still get symbols (extraction gated on `kind`, untouched) so the graph keeps them, but default search/lookup hides them. Symbol search filters `GENERATED_EXCLUSION_CLAUSE = " AND files.generated = 0"` (query/symbol.rs).

REVIEW-DRIVEN REFINEMENTS (PR #204, three Codex P2s):
- **`is_generated_path` is SEGMENT-based**, not substring: matches a `generated`/`generated-web` path SEGMENT at any depth INCLUDING repo root (`generated/x.rs`), plus `.d.ts`/`_bg.wasm.d.ts` suffixes. `contains("/generated/")` missed root-level dirs and risked false positives (`pre-generated-data/`).
- **Existing indexes need a BACKFILL.** Incremental discovery rewrites a file row only on sha/language/kind change, so a flag whose DEFINITION changed never refreshes. Gate: `GENERATED_FLAGS_VERSION` (meta key `generated_flags_version`, mirrors `graph_index_version`). `ensure_generated_flags_current` re-derives over `main.files` (NOT the non-updatable `files` UNION view — the flag is path-based, scope-independent) on a write-bearing open; read-only opens see the stale version → return None → fall back to read-write which heals once. Full rebuild stamps it via `mark_generated_flags_current`. Bump `GENERATED_FLAGS_VERSION` whenever `is_generated_path`'s definition changes again.
- **Only advertise the opt-in where it's honored.** `symbol_lookup` uses `SymbolArgs` with `SymbolInclude{Memories,Generated}`. `git_history_for_symbol`/`papertrail_for_symbol` resolve via `select_symbol` (always source-only) and never honored `include`, so they take a selector-only `SymbolRefArgs` (no `include`) — advertising a flag they'd silently ignore is a lie.

HOW TO APPLY:
- Don't filter symbol search on `files.kind` — `kind=generated` rows have no symbols; the real pollution is `kind=source` + path-heuristic. Filter on `files.generated`.
- The MCP opt-in is `symbol_lookup include: ["generated"]`. `select_one` drill-down (impact/graph/memory/history/papertrail) always excludes generated; importance/PageRank seeding passes `true` to keep generated nodes. Explicit `symbol_id`/`logical_symbol_id` bypasses the filter (only name/symbol_path SEARCH arms apply it).

title: Clone features silently return empty if the index's fingerprints predate the current NORM_VERSION — needs a new-binary `index --full`
body:
SYMPTOM: `find_clones` returns 0 classes, `clones_of_text` / the write-time clone-check hook (#287) silently no-op, and the precompute (#286) builds an empty graph — even though the index exists, is fresh, and has thousands of `symbol_fingerprints` rows.

ROOT CAUSE: every clone read path loads bags via `load_scoped_baseline_bags`, which filters `WHERE normalizer_kind='baseline' AND normalizer_version = NORM_VERSION` (currently 3, bumped in #253). An index last (re)fingerprinted by an OLDER binary has its baseline fingerprints at the old nv (1/2), so the nv=3 filter matches ZERO rows → no candidates → empty everywhere. The filter is by design (auto-exclude old-nv rows, recompute on reindex — see index/clones/mod.rs NORM_VERSION doc), but the recompute only happens when a NEW-nv binary REINDEXES a file. A background watcher running an OLD binary keeps refingerprinting at its OWN old nv, so the index never reaches nv=3 until a new-binary reindex.

DIAGNOSE: `SELECT normalizer_version, count(*) FROM symbol_fingerprints WHERE normalizer_kind='baseline' GROUP BY normalizer_version;` — 0 rows at the current NORM_VERSION is the smoking gun. (Hit live: the #287 hook no-op'd on the rag-rat self-index because it was maintained by the old 0.8.0 binary at nv≤2.)

FIX: `rag-rat index --full` with the NEW binary recomputes the active-context fingerprints at the current nv (stale nv=1/2 rows from OTHER git contexts persist but are correctly excluded). Also RESTART the MCP server/watcher after installing a binary that bumped the schema/nv — an old running watcher can't read the migrated index, and a new `index --full` leaves it schema-incompatible until restart.

LESSON: any NORM_VERSION / ALIGNMENT_VERSION bump silently disables clone recall on existing indexes until a new-binary reindex — invisible (no error, just empty results).

title: SCIP occurrence ranges are per-document position_encoding (UTF-8/16/32) — convert in byte space, never assume UTF-8
body:
The SCIP-oracle reader (`crates/rag-rat-core/src/index/oracle/scip.rs`) must read `Document.position_encoding` PER DOCUMENT and convert column offsets accordingly. SCIP `Occurrence.range` is `[start_line, start_char, end_char]` (single-line) or `[start_line, start_char, end_line, end_char]` (multi-line), and the `*_char` values count code units in the document's declared `position_encoding` — `UTF8CodeUnitOffsetFromLineStart` (bytes), `UTF16CodeUnitOffsetFromLineStart` (UTF-16 units), `UTF32`/`Unspecified` (one unit per Unicode scalar). It is declared per-`Document`, NOT globally.

THE TRAP (why this is an Invariant, not a nicety): every encoding agrees on ASCII, so a UTF-8-assuming shortcut passes every ASCII test and then SILENTLY mis-joins the moment an identifier sits after a multibyte character (an accented name, a CJK comment earlier on the line). The wrong byte offset lands on the wrong (or no) occurrence → a wrong or missing edge upgrade, with no error.

How it's handled: `LineColumnToByte` precomputes per-line byte starts, then walks one Unicode scalar at a time advancing `code_units_for(scalar, encoding)` until it has consumed `char` units, yielding an absolute BYTE offset. rag-rat edge rows store the callee identifier BYTE range (`callee_start_byte/end_byte`, #67), so the entire join works in byte space — the encoding only matters at this one conversion. `code_units_for`: UTF-8 → utf8 len; UTF-16 → 2 for astral (utf8 len 4) else 1; UTF-32/Unspecified → 1. The reader reads the document's CURRENT checkout bytes (via a `read_document_source` closure) to do the conversion; a document whose bytes can't be read is skipped (correct degradation). `local N` symbols are dropped here (`scip::symbol::is_local_symbol`). The correctness test is `oracle::tests::non_ascii_identifier_resolves_under_both_encodings` (the `café.naïve()` case under UTF-8 AND UTF-16) — keep it.

title: files.has_test_code marker set lives in 3 places that MUST match (#77 Phase 1)
body:
impact_surface's "tests touching this symbol" detection uses a precomputed `files.has_test_code` flag instead of scanning `chunks.text` for test markers (#77 Phase 1, PR #223). The marker set — `#[cfg(test)]` / `describe(` / `it(` / `test(` (the `it(`/`test(` substrings are intentionally broad; they reproduce the original `LIKE '%it(%'`/`'%test(%'` behavior, noise included) — is encoded in THREE places that must stay byte-identical, or a forward-migrated index and a freshly-indexed one disagree:

1. `index::text_has_test_marker` (crates/rag-rat-core/src/index/util.rs) — the index-time compute, called in `insert_prepared_file` from the chunk text.
2. The V024 backfill SQL in `schema::migrations::apply_files_has_test_code` — `UPDATE files SET has_test_code=1 WHERE id IN (SELECT file_id FROM chunks WHERE text LIKE '%#[cfg(test)]%' OR ...)`.
3. `test_items`'s filter (crates/rag-rat-core/src/query/impact/items.rs) reads the flag (no longer the markers directly, but its semantics assume the flag means "contains a marker").

If you change the markers, change all three. Also note: the scope VIEW `temp.files` (`lifecycle::install_scope_view`) must list `has_test_code` in BOTH its SELECT branches, or `files.has_test_code` resolves to the view and errors "no such column" (this bit during dev — the view enumerates columns explicitly, it is not `SELECT *`).

Related: the chunk-mention match in `section_like_items` + `neighbors::textual_fallback` now uses `chunk_fts MATCH` (via `impact::fts_phrase_query`), not `chunks.text LIKE` — together these mean impact_surface reads no raw `chunks.text`, the prerequisite for #77 Phase 2 (compress `chunks.text` into a `chunk_text(chunk_id, text_zstd)` sister table; sqlite-zstd is viable ON the sister table since it never gets ALTERed, unlike the evolving chunks/files).

title: #258: coherence_split GROW uses O(1) edge adjacency not sim-recompute; byte-identical when edges==≥θ set, cargo class divergence is the #271 cap inheritance
body:
WHERE: crates/rag-rat-core/src/index/clones/refine/split.rs::coherence_split (branch perf/258-coherence-split-edge-adjacency). Fixes #258.

THE CHANGE: the GROW step's per-(m,g) coherence check went from recomputing `similarity(m,g) >= theta` (an O(token_len) overlap recompute) to an O(1) HashSet edge-adjacency lookup `adjacency.contains((m.min(g), m.max(g)))` over the canonicalized `coherent_edges`. `theta` is dropped from the coherence_split signature (the edge set fully encodes the threshold). `similarity` is still consulted ONCE per edge to rank the descending-sim seed order. Net: a dense (near-)clique component is O(n^2) lookups instead of O(n^2 * token_len) recomputes. All 3 production call sites (clone_symbol_refs, find_clones, clones_for_symbol) + the in-file tests updated.

PARITY (load-bearing — read before "fixing" any apparent divergence):
- FORWARD (edge => sim>=theta) is UNCONDITIONAL: verified_clone gates `overlap >= ceil(theta*max_len)`, bit-identical to the closure's `overlap/max_len >= theta`; struct_hash edges have overlap==max_len => sim 1.0. So the new GROW NEVER admits a member the old code rejected.
- REVERSE (sim>=theta => edge) is SourcererCC admissibility, valid EXCEPT where #271's HOT_TOKEN_POSTINGS_CAP=256 drops a theta-pair sharing only hot-capped tokens (not a candidate edge even though sim>=theta). There the OLD GROW recomputes sim and RE-MERGES across that cap-dropped non-edge; the NEW GROW honors the candidate set and does not. So with the cap ON, old GROW over-merges relative to the verified candidate edges; #258 produces tighter, internally-edge-consistent classes.

EMPIRICAL PROOF (cargo bench corpus rust-lang/cargo src/cargo, 2130 clone symbols), main vs #258, SAME index:
- `clones --recall-symbols` (clean SYMBOL-level gate): BYTE-IDENTICAL, 2130 = 2130, zero diff. No symbol leaves the clone set.
- `clones --recall-signature` (CLASS-level): DIFFERS — main 1151 classes / 6008 memberships, #258 1208 classes / 4849 memberships. SAME 2130 member symbols (zero dropped/added); only the partition granularity differs.
- DECISIVE: raising HOT_TOKEN_POSTINGS_CAP to 5_000_000 (cap never fires => edges == exactly the >=theta set) in BOTH main and #258 and re-diffing recall-signature => BYTE-IDENTICAL (1693 = 1693). This proves (a) the algorithm substitution is exactly output-equivalent when edges == >=theta set, and (b) the cap-on class divergence is 100% the #271 hot-token-cap inheritance, not a #258 bug. main's GROW was silently re-merging across pairs #271 deliberately excluded as non-discriminating noise; #258 is the internally-consistent behavior.

CONSEQUENCE for reviewers: #258 does NOT introduce a new behavior class — it inherits exactly #271's already-accepted recall approximation, gated by `clones --recall-symbols` (byte-identical here). If you ever need true byte-identical class output vs pre-#271, the lever is the cap, not coherence_split. Do NOT add a sim-recompute or whole-component fallback to coherence_split to "restore" the old larger classes — that re-introduces the cap-excluded noise pairs and defeats both #271 and #258.

TESTS ADDED: coherence_split_edge_adjacency_equals_similarity_recompute_when_edges_are_theta_set (byte-identical parity pin: an inline reference_split_by_similarity_recompute reproduces the OLD per-(m,g) sim>=theta grow; asserted equal on chain/dense-clique/loose-clique/dense-minus-matching fixtures where edges==>=theta set). Kept coherence_split_grows_by_edge_adjacency_not_recomputed_similarity (divergent-direction pin). Widened coherence_split_pathological_dense_minus_matching_returns_fast ceiling 2s->10s (coarse hang-detector under nextest parallelism, not a microbench).

title: #259 fix: RANKING-only member_count dampen (1+ln_1p) on un-refined clone classes, post-refine/pre-sort in both find_clones branches
body:
WHERE: the dampen_unrefined_member_count helper (now in query_api/clones/scoring.rs after the #361 split; was clones.rs) + its TWO call sites inside find_clones (the limited and unlimited branches, each a consolidated post-refine/pre-sort pass). Fixes #259.

THE BUG (#259 Adversary C, the tail #256 left open): find_clones refines at most UNLIMITED_REFINE_BUDGET=50 classes by provisional ROI, then re-sorts the WHOLE list on the SAME ROI scale. A class still un-refined after the pass — either past the budget (idx >= 50) OR within budget but refine_class_in_place was a NO-OP (load_refine_members returned Ok(None): overlay scope, drifted source/struct_hash mismatch, parse failure, vanished hydration row) — keeps its un-refined Plan-2 ROI = cross_module_spread × member_count × body_token_len_medoid × load_bearing_factor × cohesion_min_pairwise. That product is LINEAR in member_count and carries NO coverage_roi_gate (coverage exists only post-refine). #256's gate knocks a degenerate REFINED class down ×0.10–0.70, but an UN-refined giant skips the gate, so a large refine-FAILED component out-ranks a gated refined class purely on member count.

THE FIX (RANKING-only): dampen_unrefined_member_count(&mut CandidateCloneClass) rewrites ONLY class.roi (the sort key). It divides out the linear member_count factor and multiplies in 1 + member_count.ln_1p() — the exact sub-linear shape build_class already uses for load_bearing_factor (1.0 + max_importance.ln_1p()). This preserves the other FOUR Plan-2 factors exactly without needing the refine inputs a refine-FAILED class no longer has (no medoid/spread recompute). Self-guards: `if class.refined { return }` (a refined class already went through the coverage gate in apply_refinement — never double-penalize) and `if mc <= 0.0 { return }`. member_count 2 → ~2.10 (<5% nudge); 300 → ~6.71 (~45× reduction). Monotone non-decreasing — deprioritizes the LINEAR dominance, never inverts size, never drops a class.

PLACEMENT (load-bearing): ONE consolidated `for (_, class) in built.iter_mut() { if !class.refined { dampen_unrefined_member_count(class); } }` pass in EACH branch, AFTER the refine loop (so class.refined is final) and immediately BEFORE `cs.sort_by(...)` (so it affects ranking).

WHY GATING, NOT PERF: #259 is allowed to alter the relative ORDER of returned classes; it must NOT alter which pairs are clones or class membership. The dampen touches ONLY class.roi (the sort key) — never members/membership/which-pairs.

PARITY GREEN BY CONSTRUCTION: find_clones branches into live vs precomputed ONLY at pairs_for_query / precomputed_pairs_if_eligible (returns candidate Vec<(i64,i64)>). Everything downstream — components_from_pairs, bucket_edges_by_component, coherence_split, build_class, refine_class_in_place, the new dampen + sort — is SHARED and runs identically regardless of pair source. find_clones_precomputed_matches_live compares MEMBERSHIP (order-insensitive), so a sort-key-only change is invisible to it.

clones_for_symbol and apply_refinement deliberately UNTOUCHED: clones_for_symbol returns a single class never ranked against peers; apply_refinement is the refined-only path (the gate already applies there).

FOOTGUN learned writing the e2e test: the refine cache key (refinement_key) is over the PERSISTED struct_hash + PERSISTED file sha256 (load_source_discriminators reads files.sha256 from the DB, NOT disk), so a drifted source does NOT change the key — a WARM cache hit serves the cached refinement and never re-reads disk. The drift MUST land before the VERY FIRST find_clones (cold cache) for load_refine_members to run and hit the struct_hash-faithfulness Ok(None). Do the pre-drift sanity on a throwaway index.

title: query_api/clones is a directory module: mod.rs = curated index + IndexDatabase impl; algorithm split into cohesive siblings (#361)
body:
`crates/rag-rat-core/src/index/query_api/clones/` was a single 3347-line `clones.rs` with a `clones/` submodule dir (precompute.rs, of_text.rs). #361 (branch refactor/361-clones-split) split the god-module into cohesive siblings — PURE move/reorganize, no logic change, NO re-export shim. The old `clones.rs` path is GONE.

LAYOUT (mod.rs is a curated INDEX, not the junk drawer):
- `mod.rs` — declares the submodules; owns the shared caps/thresholds several stages key off (THETA, MAX_MEMBERS, MEMBER_VALUE_CAP, HYDRATION_CHUNK, and the load-bearing `const _` assert MEMBER_VALUE_CAP < LCS_MEMBER_SAMPLE); curates the pub surface (`pub use types::{...}` — the 9 DTO types the parent query_api/mod.rs re-exports); and HOSTS the `impl IndexDatabase` query methods (candidate_clone_components, clone_symbol_refs, find_clones, refine_class_in_place [private], clones_for_symbol, load_refine_members [pub(crate)]). Methods stay on the type → ZERO external call-site changes; the compiler verifies completeness.
- `types.rs` — the public DTO/options/eligibility types + `CloneIneligibilityReason::{as_db_str,from_db_str}`.
- `substrate.rs` — SymbolBag/TokenPosting + the SourcererCC candidate-gen (candidate_pairs, candidate_pairs_from_bags, pairs_for_query, load_scoped_baseline_bags, add_struct_hash_pairs, sub_block_candidate_pairs, sub_block_tokens, sub_block_len, verified_clone, overlap, components_from_pairs, bucket_edges_by_component; consts METRIC_SAMPLE_CAP, DF_FALLBACK, HOT_TOKEN_POSTINGS_CAP). Shared substrate `precompute` + `of_text` reuse — they now `use super::substrate::{...}`.

title: #109 structure-aware reranker signal inventory: which precomputed signals attach cheaply to an RRF candidate + which correlate with the commit-replay gold
body:
Signal inventory for the model-free structure-aware reranker (#109) that reorders the RRF top-k (search/hybrid.rs::reciprocal_rank_fusion output) before return. Goal: top-3 precision (the eval's mrr_at_10 metric). Eval gold = a commit's CHANGED PATHS + derived changed symbols (commit-message query; eval.rs::replay_eval_query). KEY consequence: signals must correlate with "is this candidate's PATH/symbol one the commit touched", which makes the strongest single signal the cheapest one (path/churn), NOT the graph.

CANDIDATE HANDLE: a SearchHit already carries chunk_id, path, and symbol_path (the chunk's qualified name) — search/lexical.rs::SearchHit. Per-candidate joins on path (free) and symbol resolution (chunks.symbol_path -> active-scope symbol id, the EXISTING enrich_search_hits_with_load_bearing path in index/query_api/importance.rs) are already wired. The `importance: Option<ImportanceEnrichment>` field on SearchHit is ALREADY the scoped-weighted-fan-in enrichment — a reranker extends this seam.

SIGNAL-BY-SIGNAL (source / precomputed? / per-candidate cost / correlation with gold):

1. GIT RECENCY + CHURN per path — git_file_changes(path, commit_hash, additions, deletions) JOIN git_commits(authored_at_s/committed_at_s). NOT a per-path column; aggregated at query time exactly like query/repo_brief.rs::file_rows (commit_touch_count, recent_touch_count vs a 90-day floor newest_commit-90d). Per-candidate: one GROUP BY path join (cheap; idx_git_file_changes_path exists). CORRELATION: HIGH, possibly strongest — a commit-message query asks about active development; files a recent commit touched are exactly high-churn/recently-touched. RISK: same signal as the gold's generative process, so it can OVERFIT the replay eval and may not generalize to real "where is X" queries.

2. GLOBAL PageRank (important_symbols, query/pagerank.rs) — NOT persisted. Computed at query time: load ALL edges + power iteration; measured 0.76s over 38,578 edges live. Too slow for the hot path unless cached. A prior attempt to CACHE per-symbol PageRank was rejected because PageRank is GLOBAL but the score differs PER SCOPE (worktree overlay) so the cache had to be scope-keyed. CORRELATION: WEAK-TO-NEGATIVE — global importance favors god-modules/hubs (Config, IndexDatabase, Language), NOT what an arbitrary commit touches. VERDICT: do NOT put raw global PageRank in v1.

3. SCOPED WEIGHTED FAN-IN ("local structural load", query/load_bearing.rs) — the cheap LOCAL alternative: sum of edge_weight x confidence over the symbol's IN-edges in active scope. One bounded query per candidate symbol; ALREADY attached to SearchHit.importance. CORRELATION: WEAK (depended-upon-ness != commit-touched-ness). Use as TIE-BREAKER only.

4. SYMBOL KIND / is_test — symbols.kind + symbols.is_test (V035) + files.has_test_code (V024, precomputed). Per-candidate: free. CORRELATION: MODERATE as a DEMOTION signal — test chunks are rarely the gold for a feature commit; down-weighting is cheap and plausibly lifts top-3.

5. PATH / STRUCTURAL FEATURES — files.path, files.generated (precomputed), language. Query<->path token overlap is FREE and directly correlated with the gold (the gold IS a set of paths). generated=1 demotion free. CORRELATION: HIGH for path-token overlap (near-direct proxy for the path gold) + generated demotion.

6. CALL-GRAPH PROXIMITY to query's likely target (find_callers/trace_callees) — a graph hop (BFS), expensive, needs a NAMED target which a commit-message query lacks. CORRELATION: LOW (a commit's files are a diff, not a call neighborhood). Skip v1.

BEST BANG-FOR-BUCK (cheap AND correlated with the path/symbol gold): (a) git recency+churn per path (cheap aggregate join, highest correlation, with the overfit caveat); (b) path-token/structural match incl. generated+is_test demotion (free, near-direct proxy for the path gold); (c) scoped-weighted-fan-in as a TIE-BREAKER only (already attached, ~0 added cost). Global PageRank and call-graph proximity are the WORST bang-for-buck here: expensive AND poorly correlated with "what did this commit touch". Ship the model-free reranker FIRST with git+path+kind, A/B on the replay eval (mrr_at_10), treat any graph signal as opt-in only after a measured win.

title: Clone-graph precompute (#286): kernel validation — writer resumable/RAM-bounded, but drivers/net is pathologically θ=0.7-dense (O(K²) sub_block edges)
body:
Validated the #286 clone-graph precompute on a real `rag-rat index` of the Linux kernel drivers/net (6162 files, 118,148 fingerprints). Ran `rag-rat clones --precompute` (the Phase-B writer).

WHAT WORKED (architecture sound): the streaming generation-staged build is RESUMABLE (checkpoints cursor + edges per batch; survived two timeout kills and resumed) and RAM-BOUNDED (stayed under a 12G cgroup cap — flushes edges to disk per batch, never materializing all pairs in RAM, unlike live `find_clones` which OOM'd/hung >240s at query time). Off the query path. So for the COMMON case (cargo + normal large repos) it makes queries fast and the build tractable.

WHAT THE VALIDATION REVEALED: drivers/net is PATHOLOGICALLY clone-dense. In the first 2874 processed functions the build wrote 5.67M edges — breakdown is the key: only 4,539 are `struct_hash` (identical) edges (groups tiny, K≤11), while 5,671,293 are `sub_block` edges. So the blowup is NOT identical-clone cliques; it is θ=0.7 SIMILARITY clusters — thousands of driver functions (probe/remove/ioctl boilerplate) each ≥70% token-overlap-similar to thousands of others. An O(K²)-in-cluster-size cost INHERENT to pairwise clone detection at θ=0.7 on boilerplate code; persisting doesn't shrink it (full drivers/net graph would be tens-to-hundreds of millions of edges, a long build).

IMPLICATION: the precompute is the right architecture and a clear win for normal repos, but does NOT by itself make a pathologically-dense huge subsystem cheap — it converts a query-time OOM/hang into a long, resumable, bounded BACKGROUND job (acceptable under "mildly stale OK"). The real lever for dense code is a CLUSTER-SIZE CAP (the #271 hot-token-cap INTENT, applied at the verified-cluster level, recall-gated via #279 / `clones --recall-symbols`): once a similarity cluster exceeds a size threshold, stop materializing its full O(K²) pairwise edges (a spanning subset preserves union-find components; coherence_split's clique-cover genuinely needs the density, so the cap interacts with #256/#282 and must be recall-measured). Natural follow-up after the #286 phases land. See [[mem_19ef9c6bc90_ca78f9df6d5b]] and [[mem_19ef6c3767e_242f2636ace6]].

title: Migration "table absent at V(N-1)" test breaks when V(N) adds it; assert deferred-absence against the migration DDL in isolation, not the full ladder
#296 phase 3: CloneCorpus trait unifies the postings fast path + RAM fallback; eligibility is EXACT-freshness (R1)
body:
Phase 3 (#392, merged) makes the write-time clone check (`clones_of_text`/`clones_of_texts`, of_text.rs) read the persisted `clone_subblock_postings` instead of building the whole RAM inverted index, when eligible.

**`CloneCorpus` trait is the seam.** `CheckIndex` (RAM fallback) + `IndexedCorpus` (bounded postings fast path) expose `exact_partner_ids` + `near_candidate_bags` + `df_by_token`. The old `CheckIndex::check` became a FREE `check_against(corpus: &dyn CloneCorpus, ...)` so both modes share fingerprinting, the `verified_clone` verify, ref resolution, self-file exclusion — the fast path is a pure optimization (pinned by `fast_postings_path_equals_ram_fallback`). `load_clone_corpus` picks the mode.

**Eligibility = `IndexDatabase::clone_check_indexed_generation` (precompute.rs, `pub` for the CLI hook).** EXACT-freshness, STRICTER than the find_clones edge fast path (review R1): Complete + `normalizer_version==NORM_VERSION` + `postings_written` + `source_revision == content_revision()` EXACTLY. Because a symbol's persisted sub-block tokens depend on `sub_block_tokens`' ordering by the CURRENT `clone_token_df`; drift → silent missed near-clone. Anything less → RAM fallback.

**IndexedCorpus stays BOUNDED (R3):** near candidates from `clone_subblock_postings token_hash IN (…)` (chunked HYDRATION_CHUNK), then ONLY those anchors hydrated via row-value `(files.path, symbols.start_byte) IN (VALUES …)` over the scoped `files` view. Reproduces EVERY RAM filter (R4): scope, generated=0, is_test=0, language, NULL/corrupt token_bag skip; drops a posting whose anchor sha != current `files.sha256` (staleness); exact path adds `token_bag IS NOT NULL`.

**THREE review fixes — DO NOT regress:**
1. **Base-scope gate (footgun).** Clone graph is built in BASE scope; `content_revision()` is GLOBAL over `main.files` so can't encode scope. Under a linked-worktree OVERLAY the postings cover only base symbols while RAM reads branch-only symbols → serving the fast path silently misses overlay near-clones. `clone_check_indexed_generation` returns None when `self.active_scope_is_linked_overlay()` (lifecycle.rs: non-empty `active_worktree_id` differing from `worktree_id_of(source_root)` — NOT "empty"; base has its OWN non-empty id).
2. **Read snapshot (TOCTOU).** `with_clone_read_snapshot` wraps the whole check in one deferred read txn when idle (`is_autocommit`), so a concurrent writer completing a new generation (`complete_generation` GCs the old) mid-check can't delete the postings out from under the fast path. No-op if a txn is already open.
3. **df-freshness invalidation (subtle).** Postings freeze `sub_block_tokens`' df ordering at build. A FULL rebuild recomputes `clone_token_df` authoritatively (drift correction) WITHOUT changing content, so `content_revision()` stays equal — nothing else catches it. `refresh_clone_token_df` (rebuild.rs) now calls `invalidate_clone_graph_postings` (`UPDATE clone_graph_generations SET postings_written=0`) so the next maintenance pass rebuilds against the fresh df; the write-time check falls back to RAM until then. find_clones' edges store the verified overlap and are df-INDEPENDENT — unaffected. (Incremental df bumps ride content changes → already gated by `content_revision()`.) The rebuild.rs comment `df is selectivity-only, never a correctness input` is true for the LIVE path (both sides use the same df) but NOT the fast path (build-vs-read df split) — hence this gate.

**Incidental:** `SymbolBag`/`TokenPosting` got `#[derive(Clone)]`; `TextCloneMatch` got `PartialEq`.

**Phase 4 (#393, merged): #296 series complete.** `MAX_CLONE_CHECK_FUNCTIONS` (40k guard, claude_hook/mod.rs) is fallback-only: `clone_check` skips on size ONLY when `!db.clone_check_indexed_generation()?.is_some()`, via `clone_check_skipped_for_size(indexed, count)`. That's why `clone_check_indexed_generation` is `pub`.

title: #296 phase 2 postings size (measured): ~30 rows/function, ~164 B/row, ~0.8x clone_edges — no write-time cap in phase 2
body:
Measured the persisted `clone_subblock_postings` footprint (review R5 asked for this) on a real precompute of the rag-rat self-index (4,020 walked baseline functions, phase-2 debug binary, isolated DB copy):

- postings rows: 121,219 → avg **30.2 postings/function** (≈ |sub_block_tokens(bag, θ=0.7)| per symbol; density-INDEPENDENT — it tracks a function's distinct-token count, not how clone-dense the repo is, so ~30/fn holds on pathological corpora too).
- on-disk (dbstat): `clone_subblock_postings` = 16.34 MB table + 2.62 MB `idx_clone_subblock_postings_token` = ~19 MB. For comparison `clone_edges` (86,104 rows) = 23.83 MB. So postings ≈ **0.8× the edge table** here — NOT a blowup.
- per-row on-disk ≈ 164 B, dominated by the redundant 64-char hex `file_sha` + `path` TEXT stored inline per posting (content-anchoring, #248).
- full clone-graph rebuild (edges+postings) in DEBUG: 58 s for 4,020 functions.

Extrapolation: ~5 KB/function → ~570 MB at drivers/net's 118k-function scale (#286 memory), multi-GB for the full kernel. Large but BOUNDED to one live generation (superseded generations' postings are CASCADE-GC'd), consistent with #286's "pathological huge subsystem = long, resumable, bounded background job" contract.

DECISION: do NOT add the R5 write-time posting-list cap in phase 2. Reasons: (1) real size is comparable to clone_edges on a normal repo — non-issue for the common case; (2) a cap breaks the EXACT-parity invariant (persisted postings == `build_sub_block_index` output, pinned by `precompute_postings_match_sub_block_index`), which phase 3's fast/fallback equivalence depends on — a cap would have to be mirrored into the phase-3 read path, so co-design it THERE if ever needed; (3) if size bites at kernel scale, the higher-leverage fix is interning `file_sha`/`path` (a dictionary, like the edge string-interning #79/#224) — a bigger separate design — NOT a recall-reducing per-token cap. Stated as a real cost, not a solved one.

title: #296 phase 2: postings_written is a POSTINGS-AWARE flag set at Building creation — the R2 upgrade + leftover-Building discriminator
body:
Phase 2 (#387, merged #391) populates `clone_subblock_postings` in `reconcile_clone_edges_pass`/`flush_batch` (index/query_api/clones/precompute.rs). Non-obvious design worth not re-deriving:

**`clone_graph_generations.postings_written` semantics (the R2 gate).** Set to 1 at *Building generation CREATION* (`open_building_generation` fresh INSERT), not only at Complete. Meaning: "this generation is POSTINGS-AWARE — its postings are written in-band by a postings-aware binary." Because every walked symbol's postings are staged in the SAME transaction as its cursor advance (`flush_batch`), a postings-aware gen has postings for every symbol up to its cursor; a *Complete* postings-aware gen is therefore fully populated. So:
- `pending_clone_graph` + the Phase-0 skip read it on the LIVE (Complete) gen as "postings complete" → a pre-feature Complete gen (postings_written=0, the V037 migration default) is pending and forces ONE rebuild that fills postings (else an upgraded DB keeps an empty postings table forever).
- `open_building_generation` reads it on an existing Building gen as "resumable without a postings gap": a pre-feature leftover Building gen (postings_written=0) is DISCARDED (CASCADE drops its edges+postings) and restarted from symbol 0, NOT resumed — resuming would Complete a gen missing postings for its already-past cursor symbols (review R2 parenthetical). A new-binary Building gen (postings_written=1) resumes normally.

Why the create-time flag and NOT a "zero postings rows → discard" heuristic: the heuristic has a contrived non-convergence corner (an all-empty-sub_block_tokens prefix could loop discard→restart). The create-time flag is O(1), no false discards, no convergence risk. Safe to overload because NOTHING reads a Building gen's postings_written as "complete" — only the LIVE/Complete gen is gated (via the meta live-pointer), and `complete_generation` re-affirms postings_written=1.

**Writer mechanics (review R6):** postings emitted for EVERY walked symbol incl. zero-edge ones, before the cursor advances, INSERT OR IGNORE under the content-key PK (idempotent on resume). `PostingGroup{anchor, tokens}` clones (path, file_sha) ONCE per symbol not per token. `sub_block_tokens(bag, θ)` computed once, shared by candidate-gen and postings, so the persisted set is a byte-for-byte mirror of `build_sub_block_index` (parity test `precompute_postings_match_sub_block_index`). Mid-loop flush triggers on EITHER accumulator (`batch.len()` OR `postings.len()` ≥ batch_size) since postings are far more numerous than edges.

Phases 3 (bounded read in CheckIndex/of_text.rs) + 4 (mode-aware 40k guard) are now MERGED (#392/#393). `precomputed_pairs_if_eligible` (the find_clones EDGE fast path) deliberately does NOT check postings_written — it reads edges, which are complete for any Complete gen; only the write-time postings fast path needs the postings gate.
